subject: Indian Polity
question: Which are the two States next to U.P. having maximum representation in Lok Sabha?
explanation: Explanation: • The population of a state is the basis for allocation of seats in the Lok Sabha as per the census figures. • The total number of seats for each state was frozen at the 1971 census level by the 42nd Amendment (1976) and extended till 2026 by the 84th Amendment (2001). • Uttar Pradesh has the maximum number of seats (80). • After U.P., the states with the next highest representation are Bihar (40) and Maharashtra (48). • Madhya Pradesh and Tamil Nadu have fewer seats compared to Bihar and Maharashtra. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The members of Constituent Assembly were
explanation: Explanation: • The idea of a Constituent Assembly was first proposed by M.N. Roy in 1934 and later adopted by the Congress in 1935. • It was accepted by the British Government in the August Offer of 1940 and finally constituted under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946. • Members were indirectly elected by the provincial legislative assemblies through the single transferable vote system of proportional representation. • Representatives of princely states were nominated, but the main body was formed through indirect elections. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The Vice-President of India is elected by

options.b: The members of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
options.c: The members of Rajya Sabha only
options.d: The members of Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha and State Legislatures

explanation: Explanation: • The Vice-President is elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of both Houses of Parliament. • The election is held by the system of proportional representation through the single transferable vote, and voting is by secret ballot. • State legislatures have no role in this election, unlike the Presidential election. • According to Article 66, the Vice-President must be a citizen of India, at least 35 years old, and qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which language has been added recently to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India?
explanation: Explanation: • The 21st Amendment Act, 1967 added Sindhi to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution. • Originally, the Eighth Schedule contained 14 languages. • With the inclusion of Sindhi, the total became 15 languages. • Later amendments increased the number to 22 languages through the 71st and 92nd Amendments. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which of the following is not included in the list of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution?

options.a: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
options.b: To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
options.d: To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals

explanation: Explanation: • Fundamental Duties are listed in Article 51A, Part IVA, inserted by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976. • They include duties like respecting the Constitution, upholding sovereignty, protecting public property, promoting harmony, and preserving the environment. • “Secularism” is not a Fundamental Duty; it is part of the Preamble and reflected in various provisions of Fundamental Rights but not listed as a duty. • An additional duty regarding education for children (6–14 years) was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The President of Union of India has the same constitutional authority as the
explanation: Explanation: • India follows the parliamentary system, where the President is a nominal executive and the real powers are exercised by the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister. • This position is similar to the British Monarch, who is the ceremonial head of state but does not rule. • The President acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers, and cannot act independently in most matters. • Unlike the U.S. President, the Indian President does not enjoy executive powers personally. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: A candidate to become a member of Lok Sabha should not be less than
explanation: Explanation: • As per Article 84(b) of the Constitution, a person shall not be qualified to be chosen to fill a seat in the Lok Sabha unless he is not less than 25 years of age. • For Rajya Sabha, the minimum age requirement is 30 years. • • The candidate must also be a citizen of India and possess other qualifications prescribed by Parliament. Hence, option (b) is correct The state keeps itself separate from religious institutions, ensuring equal treatment to all religions. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which of the following is not included in Fundamental Rights in the Constitution of India?

options.c: Right to vote in all elections
options.d: Right to freedom of speech and expression

explanation: Explanation: • Right to Property was originally a Fundamental Right under Articles 19(1)(f) and 31. • It was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978, and is now a legal right under Article 300A in Part XII of the Constitution. • Right to vote is not a Fundamental Right but a constitutional right under the Representation of the People Act. • Right to freedom of religion and freedom of speech and expression continue as Fundamental Rights under Articles 25–28 and Article 19(1)(a) respectively. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Who is authorised to decide over a dispute regarding disqualification of a member of Parliament?

options.d: A committee set up by the Parliament

explanation: Explanation: • Any question regarding disqualification of a member of Parliament (other than under the Tenth Schedule) is decided by the President. • Before making a decision, the President is bound to obtain the opinion of the Election Commission, and act according to it. • In cases of anti-defection under the Tenth Schedule, the authority is the Speaker in the Lok Sabha and the Chairman in the Rajya Sabha. • The decision of the Speaker/Chairman under the Tenth Schedule is subject to judicial review. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The word ‘secular’ denotes

options.b: Freedom of religion and worship to all citizens

explanation: Explanation: • A secular state has no official religion and maintains neutrality in matters of religion. • It does not compel citizens to adopt any particular religion and does not give preferential treatment to any religious group. • In India, the word “secular” was added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, but secular principles existed in Fundamental Rights from the beginning.

subject: Indian Polity
question: The most controversial provision in the 42nd Constitution Amendment is

options.c: Term of Lok Sabha and Legislative Assemblies
options.d: Primacy to the Directive Principles over the Fundamental Rights

explanation: Explanation: • The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 gave primacy to Directive Principles of State Policy over Fundamental Rights by amending Article 31C. • It extended the protection of Article 31C to all Directive Principles, not just those in Article 39(b) and (c). • This meant that any law made to implement DPSPs could not be challenged even if it violated Articles 14, 19 or 31. • This amendment was seen as an attack on the basic structure and judicial review, making it highly controversial. • The Supreme Court in Minerva Mills case (1980) struck down this extended primacy as unconstitutional, restoring the balance between FRs and DPSPs. Hence, option (d) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The case of dispute in the Presidential election is referred to
explanation: Explanation: • Article 71 provides that all doubts and disputes related to the election of the President are decided by the Supreme Court. • The Supreme Court’s decision is final and binding. • The election cannot be challenged on the ground of an incomplete Electoral College. • If the election is declared void, acts done by the President before the declaration remain valid. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Panchayati Raj as introduced in 1959 operates at
explanation: Explanation: • The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended a three-tier Panchayati Raj system to ensure effective local selfgovernment. • Based on its recommendations, Rajasthan became the first state to launch the system on 2nd October 1959, followed by Andhra Pradesh. • The three levels are: o Village level (Gram Panchayat) o Block level (Panchayat Samiti) o District level (Zila Parishad) • This structure aimed at decentralisation of power and people’s participation in rural development. Hence, option (d) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Liberty, Equality and Fraternity, this inspiration was derived from
explanation: Explanation: • The ideals of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity were inspired by the French Revolution (1789–1799). • Liberty signifies freedom of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship. • Equality denotes the absence of special privileges and provision of equal opportunities. • Fraternity stands for a sense of brotherhood ensuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the nation. • These ideals are reflected in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: In 1980 Parliamentary elections which parties got the maximum number of seats in the descending order?

options.a: Congress (I), Lok Dal, C. P. I. (M)
options.b: Lok Dal, C. P. I. (M), Congress (I)
options.c: D. M. K., Congress (I), Lok Dal

explanation: Explanation: • The 7th General Elections were held in January 1980. • Due to internal conflicts and the split within the Janata Party, people turned back to Indira Gandhi’s Congress (I). • Congress (I) emerged as the largest party with 353 seats, followed by Lok Dal and CPI(M). • Janata Party suffered a massive defeat, winning only 31 seats. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: In which case a joint session of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha is convened by the President?

options.a: When a Finance Bill is to be passed by the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha with 2/3rd majority
options.c: If after a bill has been passed by one House and transmitted to the other House and the bill is rejected by the other House

explanation: Explanation: • A joint sitting of Parliament is convened under Article 108 to resolve a deadlock between the two Houses over an ordinary bill. • A deadlock arises when: o The bill is rejected by the other House. o The Houses disagree on amendments. o More than six months elapse without the bill being passed by the other House. • Money Bills and Constitutional Amendment Bills are not subject to joint sitting. • The Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over the joint sitting. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: 44th Amendment of the Constitution speaks of

options.a: Right to property as no longer a Fundamental Right
options.b: Suspension of individual liberty during emergency
options.c: Barring the courts from interfering in the disputes regarding the election of Prime Minister
options.d: Giving more importance to Directive Principles over Fundamental Rights

explanation: Explanation: • The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 was enacted to reverse many provisions of the 42nd Amendment made during the Emergency. • It removed the Right to Property from the list of Fundamental Rights and made it a legal right under Article 300A. • It reduced the term of the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies from six to five years. • It also introduced safeguards for declaring Emergency, requiring written advice from the Cabinet and Parliamentary approval by a twothirds majority. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The Constitution 45th Amendment Bill, passed by Parliament extended reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in Parliament and State Assemblies upto
explanation: Explanation: • The 45th Amendment Act, 1980 extended the reservation of seats for SCs and STs in Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies for another 10 years, i.e., up to 1990. • Originally, this reservation was to last for 10 years from 1950 but has been extended every 10 years through successive amendments. • The 95th Amendment Act, 2009 further extended this provision up to 2020. • The reservation applies to both Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies, but elections are held by universal adult franchise, not separate electorates. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Council of Ministers of the Union of India is responsible to the
explanation: Explanation: • Article 75(3) of the Constitution states that the Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. • This means all ministers stand or fall together; if a no-confidence motion is passed in the Lok Sabha, the entire council must resign. • The principle ensures parliamentary accountability and is a key feature of the parliamentary system of government. • Though ministers are appointed by the President, they remain in office as long as they enjoy the confidence of the Lok Sabha. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: What is the maximum period during which Parliament may not meet?
explanation: Explanation: • As per Article 85, the maximum gap between two sessions of Parliament cannot exceed six months. • This ensures that Parliament meets at least twice every year. • Typically, Parliament has three sessions annually: o Budget Session (Feb–May) o Monsoon Session (Jul–Sep) o Winter Session (Nov–Dec) • This provision maintains regular legislative oversight and prevents long gaps without parliamentary scrutiny. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Parliament consists of

options.b: President, Prime Minister and other Ministers
options.c: President, Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha
options.d: President, Chief Justice and Lok Sabha

explanation: Explanation: • Article 79 of the Constitution states that the Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses — the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha). • Though the President is not a member of either House, no bill can become a law without the President’s assent, making the President an integral part of Parliament. • The Prime Minister and Ministers are part of the executive, not Parliament itself. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Rajya Sabha can delay the Money Bill passed by the Lok Sabha for a period not exceeding
explanation: Explanation: • As per Article 109, a Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha. • After the Lok Sabha passes it, the Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject. • The Rajya Sabha must return the Money Bill within 14 days from the date of its receipt. • If not returned within this period, the bill is deemed to have been passed by both Houses in the form passed by the Lok Sabha. • Rajya Sabha cannot amend or reject a Money Bill. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The term ‘Fourth Estate’ refers to
explanation: Explanation: • The term “Fourth Estate” traditionally refers to the Press or news media, especially print journalism. • In a democracy, media acts as the fourth pillar, alongside the legislature, executive, and judiciary. • A free and independent press is essential for ensuring transparency, accountability, and public awareness. • Though the Constitution does not explicitly mention the press, its freedom is derived from Article 19(1)(a) — freedom of speech and expression. Hence, option (d) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Who was the second President of the Indian Republic?
explanation: Explanation: • Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan was the second President of India (1962–1967). • He served as the first Vice-President from 1952 to 1962 before becoming President. • He was a renowned philosopher, teacher, and statesman, and was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1954. • His birthday, 5th September, is celebrated as Teachers’ Day in India. • The first President of India was Dr. Rajendra Prasad. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which of the following High Courts covers more than one State/Union Territories?
explanation: Explanation: • The Guwahati High Court (formerly the Assam High Court) has jurisdiction over multiple North-Eastern states. • It was established in 1948 and initially served as the High Court for the entire North-East. • Currently, it exercises jurisdiction over Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram, and Arunachal Pradesh. • Separate High Courts have been created later for some UTs and states, but Guwahati remains the only High Court with multi-state jurisdiction. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The Constitution of India was actually ready in
explanation: Explanation: • The Constituent Assembly took 2 years, 11 months, and 17 days to draft the Constitution. • It was adopted on 26 November 1949, after thorough debates and discussions spread across 11 sessions. • The Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950, to commemorate the Purna Swaraj Declaration of 1930. • 26 November is now celebrated as Constitution Day in India. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Panchayati Raj System was introduced in the year
explanation: Explanation: • The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended the establishment of a threetier Panchayati Raj system — at the village, block, and district levels. • On 2nd October 1959, Rajasthan became the first state to introduce the system, followed by Andhra Pradesh nine days later. • The aim was to promote decentralisation of power and ensure people’s participation in rural development. • The system was later constitutionalised through the 73rd Amendment Act, 1992. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The dispute regarding the election of Prime Minister and President of India can be decided by
explanation: Explanation: • Disputes regarding the election of the President are decided exclusively by the Supreme Court under Article 71, and its decision is final. • For the Prime Minister, disputes are governed by the Representation of the People Act, 1951, and are dealt with by the High Courts through election petitions, not by a separate tribunal. • There is no Election Tribunal for these matters now. • Therefore, none of the given options directly matches both scenarios together. Hence, option (d) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Rajya Sabha is dissolved once in
explanation: Explanation: • The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House and is not subject to dissolution. • It was first constituted in 1952 and continues to function uninterrupted. • One-third of its members retire every two years, and new members are elected to fill those vacancies. • A member elected for a full term serves for six years. • This system ensures continuity in the legislative process, unlike the Lok Sabha which can be dissolved. Hence, option (d) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in
explanation: Explanation: • Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs) are enumerated in Part IV (Articles 36 to 51) of the Constitution. • They are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable in a court of law, but they are fundamental in the governance of the country. • Inspired by the Irish Constitution, DPSPs aim to create a welfare state by guiding the state in policy-making. • They include socialistic, Gandhian, and liberal-intellectual principles, such as promoting equal justice, organising village panchayats, and securing a uniform civil code. Hence, option (d) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: China has which type of Parliamentary System?
explanation: Explanation: • China follows a multi-party cooperation and political consultation system under the leadership of the Communist Party of China (CPC). • While the CPC is the only ruling party, there are eight other smaller political parties that participate in governance through the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC). • These parties function under the precondition of accepting CPC’s leadership, making it a multi-party system with one dominant party. • The National People’s Congress is the highest organ of state power in China. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: What does secularism mean?

options.c: State having no official religion and citizens are free to follow any religion or faith
options.d: State having one official religion and showing respect to all other religions

explanation: Explanation: • In India, secularism means that the State has no official religion and treats all religions with equal respect. • Citizens have the freedom to profess, practise and propagate any religion of their choice as guaranteed by Article 25. • The word “secular” was explicitly added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, though secular principles existed since 1950 through Fundamental Rights. • The Supreme Court in S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994) declared secularism as part of the basic structure of the Constitution. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which of the following is not a Fundamental Right?

options.d: Right to freedom of speech and expression

explanation: Explanation: • Right to Property was originally a Fundamental Right under Articles 19(1)(f) and 31, but it was removed by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978. • It is now a legal right under Article 300A, Part XII of the Constitution. • Right to equality (Articles 14–18), right against exploitation (Articles 23–24), and freedom of speech and expression (Article 19(1)(a)) continue to be Fundamental Rights. • The removal of right to property helped the State implement land reforms and social welfare legislation without legal hurdles. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: On which date Constitution of India was adopted and enacted by the Constituent Assembly?
explanation: Explanation: • The Constituent Assembly adopted and enacted the Constitution of India on 26th November 1949. • This date is mentioned in the Preamble as the day when “We, the people of India, adopted, enacted and gave to ourselves this Constitution.” • The Constitution came into effect on 26th January 1950, chosen to commemorate the Purna Swaraj declaration of 1930. • 26 November is celebrated as Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas) in India since 2015. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: President of India is elected by

options.c: Elected representatives of Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies

explanation: Explanation: • The President is elected by an Electoral College consisting of: o Elected members of both Houses of Parliament, and o Elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States, including NCT of Delhi and Puducherry. • The election is held by proportional representation through the single transferable vote system. • The value of votes is calculated based on the population of states as per the 1971 Census (frozen till 2026). • Nominated members of Parliament and State Assemblies do not participate in the election. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: How many members can be nominated to the Lok Sabha by the President?
explanation: Explanation: • As per Article 331, the President could nominate up to 2 members of the AngloIndian community to the Lok Sabha if he/she felt the community was not adequately represented. • This provision was abolished by the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019, which ended the nomination from January 2020. • The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 552:

subject: Indian Polity
question: If President wants to resign, he should address his resignation letter to the
explanation: Explanation: • As per Article 56(1)(a), the President may resign from office by writing under his hand to the Vice-President. • The President holds office for five years, but can resign earlier or be removed through impeachment. • The resignation letter takes effect from the date it is accepted. • If the office of the President falls vacant, the Vice-President acts as President until a new President is elected. Hence, option (d) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: When a money bill is passed by the Parliament, the President has the power to
explanation: Explanation: • Under Article 110, a Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha and requires the President’s prior recommendation. • Once passed by Parliament, the President cannot return a Money Bill for reconsideration. • The President must give assent, but he may withhold assent (i.e., keep it pending) — known as absolute veto. • This is different from ordinary bills, where the President has returning powers (suspensive veto). Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Directive Principles of State Policy are included in which part of the Indian Constitution?
explanation: Explanation: • Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs) are contained in Part IV of the Constitution, from Articles 36 to 51. • They are borrowed from the Irish Constitution and aim to establish social and economic democracy. • DPSPs are non-justiciable, but they are fundamental in governance, providing guidance for making laws and policies to build a welfare state. • They include socialistic, Gandhian and liberalintellectual principles. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Finance Commission is appointed for

options.d: Making recommendations to the President regarding the distribution between the Union and the States of the net proceeds of the taxes

explanation: Explanation: • The Finance Commission is a constitutional body set up under Article 280 every five years by the President. • Its main function is to recommend the distribution of tax revenues between the Union and the States and among the States themselves. • It also recommends principles governing grants-in-aid and measures to augment state finances. • It acts as the balancing wheel of fiscal federalism in India. Hence, option (d) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Panchayati Raj is mainly aimed at

options.d: Giving training to villagers for fighting elections

explanation: Explanation: • Panchayati Raj signifies the system of rural local self-government in India. • Its main aim is to decentralise power and promote political awareness and participation at the grassroots level. • It ensures people’s participation in decisionmaking for rural development. • The system was introduced after the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommendations and formally launched in 1959. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following is not a Fundamental Right?

options.b: Right to assemble peaceably and without arms

explanation: Explanation: • Originally, the Right to Property was a Fundamental Right under Articles 19(1)(f) and 31. • The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 removed it from the list of Fundamental Rights. • It is now a legal/constitutional right under Article 300A in Part XII. • Other rights such as freedom of speech (Art. 19), right to equality (Art. 14), and right to assemble (Art. 19) continue to be Fundamental Rights. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: A certain bill was passed by a State legislature in August 1982 but did not receive the assent of the State Governor. It was
explanation: Explanation: • The Bihar Press Bill, 1982 was passed by the Bihar State Legislature but the Governor did not give his assent. • The bill sought to curb indecent or scurrilous publications, making it a criminal offence to publish or possess such material. • It was seen as a serious threat to the freedom of the press, drawing widespread criticism. • Under Article 200, a Governor may give assent, withhold assent, or reserve the bill for the President’s consideration. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The regional political party which has the largest number of members in the Lok Sabha is
explanation: Explanation: • Telugu Desam Party (TDP), a regional party from Andhra Pradesh, emerged as a strong force in the early 1980s under the leadership of N.T. Rama Rao. • In the 1984 Lok Sabha elections, TDP won 30 seats, becoming the largest opposition party in the Lok Sabha at that time. • This marked a significant rise of regional parties in national politics. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The Nagaland State of India cannot be termed a State because it lacks

options.d: A High Court exclusively ‘of its own’

explanation: Explanation: • Nagaland became the 16th state of India in 1963, but like all Indian states, it does not possess sovereignty, which lies with the Union of India. • It has its own legislature and administrative structure but remains subject to the Constitution of India. • Sovereignty is the defining attribute of a state in the international sense, which Indian states, including Nagaland, do not have. • Options like linguistic homogeneity or bicameral legislature are not essential criteria for statehood under the Indian Constitution. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The reorganisation of Indian States on a linguistic basis took place in
explanation: Explanation: • The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 came into effect on 1 November 1956, reorganising the boundaries of India's states and territories primarily on linguistic lines. • It followed the recommendations of the Fazl Ali Commission (1953), which examined demands for linguistic states after the creation of Andhra State (1953) for Teluguspeaking people. • The Act divided the country into 14 states and 6 union territories. • This marked a major shift in the federal structure of India. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The greatest hallmark of personal liberty is
explanation: Explanation: • The writ of Habeas Corpus literally means “to have the body”. • It is issued by the courts to produce a person who has been detained unlawfully, ensuring protection of personal liberty. • It can be filed by any person on behalf of the detainee, making it a powerful tool against arbitrary detention. • Other writs like Mandamus, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto serve different administrative or judicial control functions. • Habeas Corpus is considered the bulwark of individual freedom in a democracy. Hence, option (d) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following is not a piece of social legislation?

options.a: The Immoral Offences and Girls Trafficking Act
options.b: The Maintenance of Internal Security Act

explanation: Explanation: • The Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA), 1971 was a law giving the government extensive powers for preventive detention, search, and wiretapping, mainly used during the Emergency (1975–77). • It was aimed at internal security and political control, not at bringing social reform. • The other Acts are social legislations: o Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 – combats trafficking and exploitation. o Abolition of Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 – enforces Article 17. o Special Marriage Act, 1954 – provides legal framework for inter-religious and civil marriages. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The Jammu and Kashmir Resettlement Bill which has stirred up controversy deals with

options.a: Reorganisation of territories between Jammu & Kashmir
options.b: Allowing people of Kashmiri origin who have migrated to Pakistan to come back to Jammu & Kashmir
options.c: Introduction of new land reforms in the State
options.d: Imposition of agricultural income tax in the State

explanation: Explanation: • The Jammu and Kashmir Resettlement Act, 1982 provided for the resettlement of persons of Kashmiri origin who migrated to Pakistan after March 1947, allowing them to return and reclaim property in J&K. • The Act became controversial due to security and citizenship concerns, as it could allow large numbers of Pakistanis (including potentially hostile elements) to enter the state. • The Supreme Court stayed the implementation of the Act, and the matter remained unresolved for years. • The Governor initially returned the Bill, but it was passed again without changes, leading to a Presidential Reference to the Supreme Court. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: It is often said that the key to the minds of the makers of our Constitution lies in
explanation: Explanation: • The Preamble embodies the philosophy, values, and objectives that guided the framers of the Constitution. • It is based on the Objectives Resolution moved by Jawaharlal Nehru in 1946. • The Supreme Court in the Berubari case (1960) observed that the Preamble is a key to open the mind of the makers of the Constitution. • It sets out the ideals of justice, liberty, equality, fraternity, and defines the nature of the Indian State as sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic. • It also serves as an interpretative tool when there is ambiguity in constitutional provisions. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Sarkaria Commission has been set up to study
explanation: Explanation: • The Sarkaria Commission was constituted in 1983 under the chairmanship of Justice R.S. Sarkaria. • It was set up to review the Centre–State relations and suggest reforms to strengthen cooperative federalism. • Key recommendations included: o Establishing a permanent Inter-State Council under Article 263. o Using Article 356 (President’s Rule) only as a last resort. o Promoting consultation with States before legislating on Concurrent List subjects. o Reactivating Zonal Councils for better coordination. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The Eighth Schedule of Indian Constitution contains

options.c: A list of 18 languages recognised by the Constitution
options.d: Number of States and Union Territories

explanation: Explanation: • The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution lists the languages recognised by the Constitution. • It originally contained 14 languages, and over time, more were added through amendments: o Sindhi was added in 1967 (21st Amendment). o Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali were added in 1992 (71st Amendment). o Bodo, Santhali, Maithili, Dogri were added in 2004 (92nd Amendment). • As of now, the total number of languages is 22. • The Government is responsible for the development of these languages under Article 351. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Match the following: A. Chief Election Commissioner B. Speaker of Lok Sabha C. Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha 1. Elected by members of Rajya Sabha 2. Appointed by the President 3. Elected by members of Lok Sabha Select the correct answer from the codes given below:
explanation: Explanation: • Chief Election Commissioner → Appointed by the President (Article 324). • Speaker of Lok Sabha → Elected by members of Lok Sabha in its first sitting by simple majority. • Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha → Elected by members of Rajya Sabha from amongst themselves. • These positions ensure the independence of constitutional bodies and the smooth functioning of Parliament. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Mandal Commission report pertains to
explanation: Explanation: • The Mandal Commission was set up in 1979 by the Janata Party Government under Prime Minister Morarji Desai, chaired by Bindheshwari Prasad Mandal. • Its purpose was to identify socially and educationally backward classes and recommend measures for their advancement. • It recommended 27% reservation in government jobs for Other Backward Classes (OBCs), so that total reservations for SCs, STs, and OBCs reached 50%. • The recommendations were implemented in 1990 by the V.P. Singh Government, which led to major political and social changes. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: A good citizen is one who is
explanation: Explanation: • A good citizen is expected to be aware of and fulfil social obligations such as respecting laws, paying taxes, and participating actively in democratic processes. • Citizenship involves both rights and duties; being socially conscious ensures harmony and collective progress. • Merely being educated or culturally rich does not ensure responsible citizenship without active contribution to society. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Centre-State financial relations are looked after by the
explanation: Explanation: • The Finance Commission, established under Article 280, is a constitutional body responsible for recommending the distribution of financial resources between the Union and the States. • It is constituted by the President every five years or earlier if necessary. • Its key functions include: o Distribution of net proceeds of taxes between the Centre and States. o Laying down the principles for grantsin-aid to States. o Recommending measures to augment State finances. • It plays a crucial role in maintaining fiscal federalism in India. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Who selects persons for appointment to the Central Civil Services in India?
explanation: Explanation: • The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), established under Articles 315–323, is the central recruiting agency for appointments to the All India Services, Central Services, and services of Union Territories. • It conducts various competitive examinations such as Civil Services Examination, Engineering Services, etc. • While the President makes the formal appointment, the selection is carried out by UPSC, ensuring independence, meritocracy, and transparency in recruitment. • UPSC is a constitutional body, independent of the executive. Hence, option (d) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Panchayati Raj system was adopted to

options.d: To introduce a form of local self-government at the village, block and district levels

explanation: Explanation: • The Panchayati Raj system was adopted to promote decentralisation of power and strengthen grassroots democracy. • It aims to transfer decision-making powers from the Centre and States to local bodies, enabling people’s participation in governance. • Based on the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommendations, the system was first implemented in 1959 in Rajasthan. • Later, the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 gave it constitutional status, mandating a three-tier structure — village, block, and district levels. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Democracy exists in India. Government is run by the elected representatives of the people. For proper functioning of this system

options.a: One should cast vote in elections
options.b: One must be prompt in paying taxes
options.c: One must be good to himself and to the society

explanation: Explanation: • Democracy functions effectively only when citizens actively participate in elections by exercising their right to vote. • Voting enables people to choose their representatives, hold them accountable, and shape the direction of governance. • While paying taxes and being socially responsible are important civic duties, voting is the primary mechanism through which democracy operates in a representative system like India. • Universal adult franchise is the foundation of India’s democratic structure. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Opposition conclave at Srinagar forwarded the following recommendations: A. Government at the Centre should be shared by all parties B. Governor should be appointed from a panel forwarded by the State Government concerned C. Setting up of Inter-State Council to finalise disputes between the states D. Giving more powers to the States E. Articles 356 and 357 should be suitably amended F. Resignation of Central Government Out of these only:

options.b: A, C and D are true
options.c: C, D, E and F are true

explanation: Explanation: • The Opposition Conclave at Srinagar (1983– 84) was held to highlight issues of CentreState relations and the dominance of the Centre in Indian federalism. • Key demands included: o Sharing power at the Centre among all parties to prevent centralisation. o Appointment of Governors from a panel suggested by the respective State Government to reduce bias. • Other options like amendments to Articles 356/357 or creation of Inter-State Council were discussed later in different forums like the Sarkaria Commission. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which is correct?

options.a: Lok Sabha cannot be dissolved before 5 years
options.b: Rajya Sabha lasts only for 6 years
options.c: Lok Sabha can be dissolved before 5 years
options.d: Life of Lok Sabha can be extended indefinitely

explanation: Explanation: • The normal term of the Lok Sabha is 5 years from the date of its first sitting (Article 83). • However, the President can dissolve the Lok Sabha earlier on the advice of the Council of Ministers, or if no government can be formed. • During a national emergency, Parliament may extend the term of Lok Sabha by one year at a time, but not beyond 6 months after the emergency ends. • The Rajya Sabha, on the other hand, is a permanent house and is not subject to dissolution; one-third of its members retire every 2 years. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following States with respect to their representation to the Lok Sabha: I. Andhra Pradesh II. Madhya Pradesh III. Tamil Nadu IV. Maharashtra Which of the following sequences is correct? (> means greater than)
explanation: Explanation: • Allocation basis: Seats are allotted broadly in proportion to population, and the numbers were frozen at 1971 census levels (42nd & 84th Amendments) till 2026. • Seat counts (historical/frozen): Maharashtra 48, Andhra Pradesh 42 (pre-bifurcation), Tamil Nadu 39, Madhya Pradesh 29 (preChhattisgarh). • Why not others: TN (39) is lower than AP (42), and MP (29) is lowest among the four, so any order putting MP before TN/AP is wrong. • Correct descending order: Maharashtra (IV) > Andhra Pradesh (I) > Tamil Nadu (III) > Madhya Pradesh (II). Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The President of India is elected indirectly by the electoral college consisting of the elected members of the

options.c: Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha only
options.d: Lok Sabha, the Rajya Sabha and the Legislative Assemblies of the States

explanation: Explanation: • Electoral College: Elected members of both Houses of Parliament + elected MLAs of all States and of NCT of Delhi & Puducherry. • Excluded: Nominated members (both at Centre and States) do not vote in the Presidential election. • Voting system: Proportional Representation by Single Transferable Vote; secret ballot. • Vote value equalisation: Formula ensures uniformity among States and parity between States and the Union (Article 55). Hence, option (d) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: In which of the following States in India, the number of electorate is the highest?
explanation: Explanation: • Electorate means the total number of registered voters; it correlates strongly with population. • Uttar Pradesh is India’s most populous state, therefore it has the largest voter list. • Bihar, Rajasthan, Karnataka have smaller populations/electorates than U.P., so they trail behind. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: In a Parliamentary System of Government

options.a: The parliament is responsible to the executive
options.b: The parliament is responsible to the judiciary
options.c: The executive is responsible to the parliament
options.d: The judiciary is responsible to the parliament

explanation: Explanation: • Core doctrine: Collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha (Article 75(3)). • Practical control tools: Question Hour, Zero Hour, censure & no-confidence motions, calling attention, adjournment motions, committee oversight. • Consequence: If the ministry loses majority or a no-confidence motion passes, it must resign or seek dissolution. • Why others are wrong: Parliament isn’t responsible to the executive/judiciary; judiciary reviews legality, not policy. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: After retirement, a High Court Judge

options.a: Can plead in the same High Court
options.b: Cannot plead in the same High Court
options.c: Can plead in the Supreme Court
options.d: Can plead in any of the High Courts

explanation: Explanation: • Article 220: A permanent High Court judge, after retirement, shall not plead or act in the High Court in which he served (to avoid conflict of interest and maintain impartiality). • Permissible practice: Such a retired judge may appear in the Supreme Court or in other High Courts (but not the same one). • Trap in options: While (c) and (d) mention where they can practise, the question asks what is barred; hence the correct choice is the prohibition. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The Panchayati Raj was first introduced in the States of
explanation: Explanation: • Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended a three-tier Panchayati Raj for grassroots democracy. • Inauguration: 2 October 1959, Nagaur (Rajasthan) by Jawaharlal Nehru. • Second state: Andhra Pradesh, 9 days later at Shadnagar. • Constitutional status: Later entrenched via the 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992), adding Part IX & Eleventh Schedule. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which of the following languages are included in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
explanation: Explanation: • The Eighth Schedule originally contained 14 languages, and over the years, more were added through Constitutional Amendments. • Sindhi was added by the 21st Amendment Act, 1967. • Kashmiri, Konkani and Nepali were added by the 71st Amendment Act, 1992. • English is not listed in the Eighth Schedule — it's an official language, but not a scheduled language. • Therefore, the correct combinations from the given options are: o (c) Kashmiri and Konkani o (d) Sindhi and Kashmiri Hence, options (c) and (d) are correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains

options.b: Salaries of the President, Governors of States, Judges of Supreme Court, etc.
options.c: Union List, State List and Concurrent List
options.d: Allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha

explanation: Explanation: • Seventh Schedule provides for three-fold distribution of legislative subjects between the Centre and the States: o List I – Union List (currently 100 subjects): Parliament has exclusive power (e.g., defence, banking, foreign affairs). o List II – State List (currently 61 subjects): States have exclusive power in normal times (e.g., police, public health, agriculture). o List III – Concurrent List (currently 52 subjects): Both Parliament and States can legislate; in case of conflict, Parliament’s law prevails (e.g., criminal law, marriage & divorce, education). • This division is inspired by the Government of India Act, 1935 and ensures a federal legislative structure. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The National Anthem was written by
explanation: Explanation: • “Jana Gana Mana” was originally composed in Bengali by Rabindranath Tagore. • It was first sung on 27 December 1911 at the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress. • It was adopted as the National Anthem by the Constituent Assembly on 24 January 1950. • The full song has five stanzas; the playing time of the full version is approximately 52 seconds. • Tagore himself translated the song into English. • (b) Bankim Chandra wrote “Vande Mataram”, not Jana Gana Mana. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: What is the minimum percentage of the strength of opposition required in a State legislature for the appointment of an opposition leader?
explanation: Explanation: • There is no specific constitutional or legal requirement for a minimum percentage for appointment of a Leader of Opposition. • However, by parliamentary convention, a party must secure at least 10% of the total strength of the House to get official recognition as the Opposition Party and thereby have a Leader of the Opposition. • If no party meets this criterion, no formal Leader of the Opposition is appointed. • This rule applies both at the Union and State levels. Hence, option (d) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Who among the following is/are member(s) of Parliament? A. Shivaji Ganesan B. Amitabh Bachchan C. Sunil Dutt D. Vyjayanthimala E. Jayalalitha

options.b: B, C, D and E only
options.c: All of A, B, C, D and E
options.d: A, B, C and D only

explanation: Explanation: • Shivaji Ganesan → Nominated to Rajya Sabha in 1982 after the death of Nargis. • Amitabh Bachchan → Elected to Lok Sabha from Allahabad in 1984 on a Congress ticket with record victory margin. • Sunil Dutt → Elected to 8th Lok Sabha from Mumbai North-West on Congress ticket. • Vyjayanthimala → Elected twice to Lok Sabha and once nominated to Rajya Sabha. • Jayalalitha → Elected as Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha) before becoming CM of Tamil Nadu. All five have served in Parliament at some point. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The most irritating factor in the Centre–State relationship is the

options.b: Interference of the Centre in the functions allotted to them by the Constitution

explanation: Explanation: • River water disputes are generally interstate, not between Centre and States directly. The Centre usually acts as arbitrator (e.g., Cauvery, Krishna). • Financial allocation is guided by the Finance Commission (Art. 280), a constitutional body, reducing scope for arbitrary interference. • The real friction arises when the Centre interferes in State matters—especially through provisions like: o Article 356: Imposition of President’s Rule, often on political grounds. o Article 249 & 250: Parliament legislating on State List matters in national interest or during emergencies. o Governor’s discretionary powers, often seen as an agent of the Centre. • These central interventions have historically been major irritants in Centre–State relations. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Mandamus means

options.a: A writ issued by a superior court commanding that a specified thing be done
options.b: A legal term for a prisoner’s right to appear in person and be tried in court
options.c: A written public declaration of the intentions, opinions or motives of a sovereign or of a leader, party or body
options.d: The principle of hybridisation, discovered by Gregor Mendel which led to the improved breeds of plant and animal life

explanation: Explanation: • Mandamus literally means “We command”. • It is issued by a higher court to a public authority, corporation, tribunal, or inferior court, directing them to perform a public/legal duty which they have failed or refused to perform. • It is called a “wakening call” — it wakes up authorities from inaction. • Limitations: It cannot be issued against: o Private bodies, o The President or Governors, o Chief Justices acting in judicial capacity, o To enforce non-statutory departmental instructions, or o When duty is discretionary. • It is one of the five writs under Article 32 & 226. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The main function of the National Development Council is

options.c: To review the working of the National Plan from time to time

explanation: Explanation: • National Development Council (NDC) was set up in August 1952 by an executive resolution, not by the Constitution. • Composition: PM (Chairman), Union Ministers, Chief Ministers, Lt. Governors of UTs, and members of the Planning Commission. • Main functions: o Prescribe guidelines for the preparation of National Plan. o Consider and approve the National Plan. o Assess resources required for the Plan. o Consider policy questions affecting national development. o Review the working of the Plan from time to time. o Recommend measures for achieving Plan targets. • It served as a bridge between the Centre and States in planning. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Sarkaria Commission was set up to

options.a: Investigate about the riots that took place in Delhi in 1984
options.c: Make necessary investigations and suggestions regarding the problem of Punjab
options.d: Investigate about the assassination of Mrs. Indira Gandhi

explanation: Explanation: • Sarkaria Commission was constituted in 1983 under Justice R.S. Sarkaria to review Centre– State relations and recommend reforms. • Key recommendations: o Set up a permanent Inter-State Council (Article 263) → later implemented. o Use Article 356 sparingly. o Promote consultation with States before legislating on Concurrent List. o Strengthen Zonal Councils. • It was not related to Punjab, riots, or Indira Gandhi’s assassination. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Asom Gana Parishad was recently in the news because

options.a: Of the 64 elected members, 52 are bachelors
options.b: All the 64 legislators are in the age group of 25 to 35
options.c: All the legislators have been elected for the first time

explanation: Explanation: • Asom Gana Parishad (AGP) emerged from the six-year-long Assam Movement (1979–1985) led by AASU & AAGSP, demanding detection and deportation of illegal migrants. • After the Assam Accord (1985), AGP contested the state elections in December 1985 and won a landslide, forming the government. • Notable facts about AGP MLAs: o Majority were young first-time legislators. o Many were bachelors. o All belonged to 25–35 age group, marking a generational shift in Assamese politics. • Prafulla Kumar Mahanta, aged 33, became India’s youngest CM at the time. Hence, option (d) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The Directive Principles of State Policy have been given precedence over Fundamental Rights in the .... Constitutional Amendment
explanation: Explanation: • The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 is also called the “Mini Constitution” because of its wide-ranging changes. • It gave Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV) precedence over certain Fundamental Rights (Part III), particularly those under Articles 14 and 19. • A new clause was added to Article 31C, providing that no law implementing any of the Directive Principles could be declared invalid on the ground of violating Articles 14 or 19. • Although the Supreme Court in Minerva Mills (1980) struck down the extension of Article 31C to all DPSPs, it upheld the basic precedence of Article 39(b) & (c) DPSPs over FRs. • This reflected the intention to promote social and economic justice over individual rights in certain contexts. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which of the following is correct about the Chief Election Commissioner? He holds the office till he attains the age of

options.c: 62 years or completes 3 years of service, whichever is earlier
options.d: 65 years of age or completes 5 years of service, whichever is earlier

explanation: Explanation: • The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and other Election Commissioners are appointed by the President under Article 324. • They hold office for 6 years or until they attain the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier. • They enjoy security of tenure — removal only like a Supreme Court judge (by a special majority resolution of Parliament on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity). • Their conditions of service cannot be varied to their disadvantage during tenure. • They do not hold office “during the pleasure of the President” despite being appointed by him. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which of the following States are not covered by the Panchayati Raj?
explanation: Explanation: • Meghalaya and Nagaland are not covered by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, which provides for the constitutional status of Panchayati Raj Institutions. • This exclusion is due to their distinct tribal traditions, customary laws, and existing local governance systems protected under Sixth Schedule and Article 371A. • Sixth Schedule provides for Autonomous District Councils, particularly in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. • Nagaland’s local self-government works through traditional tribal institutions. • Other North-Eastern states like Tripura and Assam are covered by Panchayati Raj provisions. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which of the following is a ‘cognizable offence’?

options.a: First offence committed by any person
options.d: Offence which can be dealt with by the court

explanation: Explanation: • As per Section 2(c) of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973, cognizable offences are those where a police officer can arrest without a warrant and start investigation without the magistrate’s permission. • These are serious offences, such as murder, rape, dowry death, kidnapping, theft, etc. • In contrast, non-cognizable offences require a warrant and prior permission from a magistrate for investigation (e.g., defamation, public nuisance). • The phrase “dealt with by the court” here refers to offences under regular judicial procedure, not private complaints. Hence, option (d) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: A Parliamentary bill passed by the Lok Sabha is sent to the President for assent. The President sends it back to Lok Sabha for reconsideration. If the Lok Sabha again sends it back to the President without making any changes, the President

options.a: Must give his assent to it
options.b: Can again send the bill for reconsideration
options.c: Can take help of the Supreme Court

explanation: Explanation: • Article 111 governs the President’s powers regarding ordinary bills: o The President may give assent, or withhold assent, or return the bill (if not a Money or Constitutional Amendment Bill) for reconsideration. • If the bill is passed again by Parliament, with or without changes, and sent to the President the second time, the President is constitutionally bound to give assent. • The President cannot return it again nor refer it to the Supreme Court nor call a referendum. • This ensures that Parliament’s will ultimately prevails and prevents a deadlock between the legislature and the executive. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The Institute of Ombudsman was first established in
explanation: Explanation: • The word “Ombudsman” is of Swedish origin, meaning “grievance person”. • The modern concept originated in Sweden in 1809, when the Swedish Parliament established the office of Justitieombudsman to safeguard citizens against administrative injustices. • Functions of the Swedish Ombudsman include: o Addressing abuse of administrative discretion. o Investigating maladministration, corruption, nepotism, and official discourtesy. • The Ombudsman system has since been adopted by many countries, including India in the form of Lokpal and Lokayuktas (Lokpal Act, 2013). Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: India is a federal state because of

options.c: Share of power between the Centre and the States

explanation: Explanation: • Federalism is characterised by division of powers between two levels of government — Central and State — each constitutionally independent in its sphere. • In India: o Legislative powers are divided into Union, State, and Concurrent Lists (Seventh Schedule). o Executive and financial powers are similarly divided. o There are independent constitutional mechanisms (e.g., Finance Commission, Inter-State Council) to manage this division. • Dual citizenship does not exist in India (unlike the USA). • Dual judiciary isn’t an accurate feature (India has a single integrated judiciary). • A written constitution (option d) is a characteristic, but not the defining reason for federalism. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Governor of which State has been entrusted with the special powers for the administration of tribal areas?
explanation: Explanation: • Sixth Schedule of the Constitution contains special provisions for the administration of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. • In these states, certain tribal areas are designated as Autonomous Districts with District and Regional Councils, enjoying legislative, administrative and judicial powers. • The Governor of Assam plays a key role: o He can organise and reorganise autonomous districts, alter their boundaries, or change names. o He also has oversight powers over laws passed by District Councils. • These powers are unique to Assam’s Governor and not found in Bihar, MP, or Arunachal Pradesh. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The Speaker of the lower house of a State can step down by submitting his resignation to the
explanation: Explanation: • The Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly holds office until the House is dissolved or he resigns or is removed by a resolution of the Assembly (Article 178–181). • He may resign by writing to the Deputy Speaker (similar to the Lok Sabha Speaker who resigns to the Deputy Speaker). • Removal requires a majority of all the then members of the House with 14 days’ notice. • The Speaker does not resign to the Governor or CM. • When a removal resolution is under consideration, the Speaker cannot preside over the House but may participate and vote. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: India has Parliamentary democracy system because

options.a: Members of the Lok Sabha are elected by the public
options.b: Council of Ministers is responsible to the Legislature
options.c: Of distribution of power between the Centre and the States

explanation: Explanation: • India has adopted the Parliamentary system of government, both at the Centre (Articles 74–75) and in the States (Articles 163–164). • The key feature of the parliamentary system is collective responsibility of the executive to the legislature: o The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. o If the Lok Sabha passes a noconfidence motion, the entire council resigns. • Other features: o Real executive is the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister, while the President is nominal executive. o There is fusion of powers between the executive and legislature. • Option (a) is a feature of representative democracy, not specifically parliamentary system. • Option (c) is related to federalism, not parliamentary form. • Option (d) is too broad and not the core reason. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Judges of a High Court are appointed by the President with the consent of the

options.b: Governor, the Chief Justice of India and the Chief Justice of the High Court concerned
options.c: Governor and the preceding Chief Justice of the High Court

explanation: Explanation: • Article 217: The President appoints High Court judges after consultation with: o The Chief Justice of India, o The Governor of the concerned State, and o In the case of appointment of a judge (other than Chief Justice), the Chief Justice of that High Court. • Chief Justice of a High Court is appointed after consultation with the Chief Justice of India and the Governor. • Second Judges Case (1993): Supreme Court held that CJ of India’s opinion has primacy. • Third Judges Case (1998): Appointment must be through collegium (CJI + 2 senior-most SC judges). • This ensures judicial independence, preventing executive dominance in appointments. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Parliament can legislate matters in the State List

options.b: If Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by 2/3rd majority
options.d: By asking the legislature of the State concerned

explanation: Explanation: • Article 249: Parliament can legislate on State List matters if the Rajya Sabha, by a 2/3rd majority of members present and voting, declares it is necessary in the national interest. o The resolution remains valid for one year, renewable annually. • Other circumstances where Parliament can legislate on State List: o Article 250: During a National Emergency. o Article 252: When two or more States pass resolutions requesting Parliament to legislate. o Article 253: To implement international treaties. o Article 356: During President’s Rule in a State. • It is not dependent on President’s wish, nor can it be done under any circumstances. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The maximum gap between two sessions of the Parliament can be of
explanation: Explanation: • Article 85: The President summons each House of Parliament from time to time, but six months must not intervene between its last sitting in one session and the date appointed for its first sitting in the next session. • This ensures regular parliamentary oversight on the executive. • Parliament usually meets in three sessions each year: o Budget Session (Feb–May) Monsoon Session (July–Aug) o Winter Session (Nov–Dec) • A gap of more than six months would violate the Constitution. Hence, option (a) is correct o

subject: Indian Polity
question: First non-Congress government to come in power in any Indian State is

options.b: Communist Party of India in Kerala

explanation: Explanation: • In 1957, the Communist Party of India (CPI) won the Kerala Assembly elections, forming the first non-Congress state government in India. • E.M.S. Namboodiripad became the first Communist Chief Minister. • This was historic because: o It was the first democratically elected Communist government in the world. o It marked the end of Congress’s monopoly in state politics. • DMK came to power in Tamil Nadu only in 1967. • CPI(M) in West Bengal came later, in 1977. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: A political party is recognised as a national party

options.a: When it contests elections in all the States of the country.
options.b: When it secures at least five per cent of the total votes cast in a national election.
options.c: If it captures power at least in three States.
options.d: If it is recognised as a political party in four or more States.

explanation: Explanation: • As per the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968, issued by the Election Commission of India, a political party can be recognised as a national party if it satisfies any of the following conditions: o It wins 2% of seats in the Lok Sabha (i.e., at least 11 seats) from 3 different States, or o It secures 6% of valid votes in four or more States in a Lok Sabha or Assembly election and wins 4 Lok Sabha seats, or o It is recognised as a State party in four or more States. • Recognition gives parties privileges like reserved symbols, free airtime on media, consultation in setting election dates, etc. • Contesting in all states (a) is not mandatory. Capturing power in three states (c) is not a criterion. Hence, option (d) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The Constitution of India provides for the nomination of two members to the Lok Sabha by the President to represent

options.a: Men of eminence in arts, letters, science, etc.

explanation: Explanation: • Article 331 of the Constitution empowered the President to nominate up to two members of the Anglo-Indian community to the Lok Sabha if he/she is of the opinion that the community is not adequately represented. • The aim was to safeguard the interests of the Anglo-Indian community, a small minority. • Originally, the Lok Sabha could have 530 elected members from states, 20 from UTs, and 2 nominated Anglo-Indian members. • Note: The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019 abolished this nomination from January 25, 2020. • Eminent persons (a) are nominated to Rajya Sabha under Article 80. Hence, option (d) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The allocation of seats for each State in the present Lok Sabha is based on the
explanation: Explanation: • Article 82 provides for readjustment of Lok Sabha seats after every Census through a Delimitation Act. • The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 froze the allocation of Lok Sabha seats to the states based on the 1971 Census, to encourage population control measures. • This freeze was extended by the 84th Amendment Act (2001) up to 2026. • The 87th Amendment allowed delimitation of constituencies using the 2001 Census, but without altering the number of seats per state. • Thus, the 1971 Census remains the basis for the allocation of seats in Lok Sabha. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Who among the following have a right to vote in the Vice-Presidential election but not in the Presidential election?

options.a: Ministers who are not members of either House of the Parliament
options.b: Elected members of the Upper Houses of the States
options.d: Members of the Parliament who abstain from all meetings of the House for a period of sixty days without permission of the House

explanation: Explanation: • Vice-President is elected by an Electoral College consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament (Article 66). o It includes elected as well as nominated members of Parliament. • President is elected by elected MPs + elected MLAs of all states and UTs with legislatures (Article 54). o Nominated members do not vote in the Presidential election. • So, nominated members of Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha have the right to vote for VicePresident, but not for President. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: It is for any economic consideration involving loss of freedom of contract leading to forced employment. Choose the correct answer from the codes given below:
explanation: Explanation: • Article 23 of the Constitution prohibits traffic in human beings, begar (forced labour) and other similar forms of forced labour. • The term ‘begar’ means compulsory work without remuneration, historically prevalent under feudal systems. • The prohibition includes economic compulsion — forcing someone to work for less than minimum wage amounts to forced labour. • The Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act further reinforced this prohibition by abolishing bonded labour agreements. • Any contravention is punishable by law. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Assertion (A): The Indian Constitution closely follows the British Parliamentary model. Reason (R): In India the Upper House of the Parliament has judicial powers.

options.a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true but R is NOT a correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true but R is false
options.d: A is false but R is true

explanation: Explanation: • Assertion (A) is true: India adopted the British Parliamentary System, characterised by: o Nominal and real executives, o Collective responsibility of the executive, o Leadership of PM, o Fusion of powers. • Reason (R) is false: The Rajya Sabha (Upper House) does not have judicial powers; only the Judiciary has that role. o Rajya Sabha has legislative, deliberative, and some special powers (e.g., Art. 249), but no judicial functions. • Therefore, while the assertion is correct, the reason is wrong. Hence, option (c) is correct o If the total strength of the Lok Sabha is 545, then absolute majority = 273 (50% + 1). • This majority is usually required for: o Formation of government in Lok Sabha. o No-confidence motions. o Removal of Speaker or Deputy Speaker. • It is different from: o Effective majority → majority of effective strength (total strength – vacancies). o Special majority → used for constitutional amendments, varies by article. o Simple majority → more than 50%

subject: Indian Polity
question: Absolute majority means _____ per cent of votes.
explanation: Explanation: • Absolute majority means more than 50% of the total membership of a House — not just those present and voting. • Example:

subject: Indian Polity
question: The first Leader of the opposition to get recognition in the Indian Parliament was
explanation: Explanation: • In India, the Leader of the Opposition is the leader of the largest Opposition party having at least 1/10th of the total seats in the House. • The position was formally recognised in 1969. • Ram Subhag Singh, a senior Congress leader from Bihar who later joined Congress (O), was recognised as the first official Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha in 1969. • Later, Y. B. Chavan (1977–1979) became one of the most prominent Leaders of Opposition. • The Leader of Opposition was given statutory status in 1977, entitling them to salary, allowances and facilities equivalent to a Cabinet Minister. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Cognizable offence refers to an offence where

options.a: Arrests can be made without warrant.
options.b: Arrests can be made with warrant.
options.c: It is under the jurisdiction of a court.
options.d: Police can register a case without formal complaint.

explanation: Explanation: • Section 2(c) of CrPC (1973): o Cognizable offences are those where police can arrest without warrant and start investigation without prior approval of a magistrate. • Examples: murder, rape, kidnapping, dowry death, theft, etc. • Police can register FIRs suo motu, i.e., even without a formal complaint. • Non-cognizable offences require a warrant and magistrate’s permission for investigation. • Option (a) is partially correct, but option (d) captures the core legal definition more precisely. Hence, option (d) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: No money bill can be introduced in the legislative assembly without the recommendations of the
explanation: Explanation: • Under Article 207, a Money Bill can be introduced only in the Legislative Assembly, not in the Legislative Council (if present), and only on the recommendation of the Governor. • Every Money Bill is considered a Government Bill and can only be introduced by a Minister. • Once passed by the Assembly, the Bill is sent to the Council (if applicable), which has limited powers — it cannot reject or amend, only recommend, and must return it within 14 days. • Ultimately, the Legislative Assembly has overriding powers regarding a Money Bill. • The Governor can assent, withhold assent, or reserve the bill for President, but cannot return it for reconsideration. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which among the following is not a part of electoral reforms?
explanation: Explanation: • Electoral reforms in India aim to make elections free, fair, and transparent. • Some key reforms: o Registration of political parties under Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951. o Disqualification of candidates involved in electoral malpractices or criminal offences. o Introduction of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) in 1998 to curb booth capturing and improve efficiency. • The appointment of Election Commissioners is governed by Article 324 of the Constitution and is not itself an electoral reform — it's a constitutional mechanism. Hence, option (d) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Parliament or a State Legislature can declare a seat vacant if a member abstains himself without permission from the sessions for at least
explanation: Explanation: • Article 101(4) (for Parliament) and Article 190(4) (for State Legislatures): o If a member is absent from all meetings for 60 days or more, without permission, his seat may be declared vacant. • The period of sixty days excludes any period when the House is prorogued or adjourned for more than four consecutive days. • This provision ensures accountability and discourages absenteeism among elected representatives. • Similar provisions are included in the Rules of Procedure of both Houses. Hence, option (b) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Assertion (A): Panchayati Raj institutions were set up to decentralise planning to village level. Reason (R): Village panchayats are in a better position to have a proper appreciation of their developmental needs.

options.a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true but R is false
options.d: A is false but R is true

explanation: Explanation: • Assertion (A): True. The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) to ensure decentralised governance and participatory democracy. • Reason (R): True. Village Panchayats directly engage with people and can better assess local needs, resources, and developmental priorities compared to distant centralised bodies. • The Act included: o Three-tier system (village, block, district), o Reservation of seats for SCs/STs/Women, o 11th Schedule with 29 subjects for Panchayats, o Establishment of State Election Commissions and State Finance Commissions. • Thus, both statements are true and R explains A correctly. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following statements regarding a No-confidence Motion in the Parliament: 1. There is no mention of a No-confidence Motion in the Constitution of India. 2. A period of six months must elapse between the introduction of one No-confidence Motion and the other. 3. At least 100 members must support a Motion of No-confidence before it is introduced in the House. 4. A motion of No-confidence can be introduced in the Lok Sabha only. Of these statements:
explanation: Explanation: • Statement 1: Correct. The Constitution does not mention No-confidence motions. It is a parliamentary practice derived from Rules of Procedure (Rule 198, Lok Sabha). • Statement 2: Incorrect. There is no such restriction of 6 months between two noconfidence motions. • Statement 3: Incorrect. Only 50 members must rise in support for it to be admitted, not 100. • Statement 4: Correct. A No-confidence Motion can be introduced only in Lok Sabha, since the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (Article 75). • If passed by a simple majority, the Council of Ministers must resign. Hence, option (d) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: The value of a vote of a member of the Parliament for the election of the President of India is determined by dividing the

options.a: Nation’s population as per the latest census by the number of Lok Sabha members
options.b: Population as per the latest census by the total strength of the two Houses of the Parliament
options.c: The total value of votes of the members of all the State Legislative Assemblies by the elected members of the two Houses of the Parliament
options.d: Particular State’s population as per the latest census by the number of members of Parliament elected from that State
