explanation: Explanation: • Article 55 of the Constitution lays down the procedure for calculating the value of votes for Presidential elections: o The value of votes of MLAs = (Population of the state / Number of elected MLAs) ÷ 1000. o The value of votes of MPs = Total value of votes of all MLAs of all States÷Total nu mber of elected MPs (LS + RS)\text{Total value of votes of all MLAs of all States} \div \text{Total number of elected MPs (LS + RS)}Total value of votes of all MLAs of all States÷Total number of elected MPs (LS + RS) • This ensures uniformity in the scale of representation of different states and parity between states and the Union. • Nominated MPs do not participate in the Presidential election. • The latest census used is the 1971 Census, as the seat allocation and vote values have been frozen until 2026. Hence, option (c) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Assertion (A): Equality before the law is not applicable to the President of India Reason (R): The President of India enjoys special powers and privileges under the Constitution

options.a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true but R is false
options.d: A is false but R is true

explanation: Explanation: • Article 14 guarantees equality before law and equal protection of laws. However, this is not absolute — the Constitution itself creates exceptions. • The President of India enjoys constitutional immunities under Article 361: o No criminal proceedings shall be instituted during their term. o No arrest or imprisonment shall be issued against the President. o No answerability to any court for acts done in the exercise of official powers. o Civil proceedings can be initiated only after due notice. • These privileges are to protect the dignity and functioning of the highest constitutional office, not to grant personal impunity. • Thus, both A and R are true and R correctly explains A. Hence, option (a) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Holding of elections for the Panchayats is decided by
explanation: Explanation: • The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 inserted Part IX (Articles 243–243O) into the Constitution, giving constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions. • Article 243K: o The superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of Panchayat elections is vested in the State Election Commission (SEC). o The SEC is headed by a State Election Commissioner, appointed by the Governor, and enjoys security of tenure similar to High Court judges. • Neither the District Magistrate nor the State Government conducts these elections. • The Election Commission of India conducts elections for Parliament and State Legislatures, not Panchayats. Hence, option (d) is correct

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following statements regarding the election of the President of India is correct?

options.a: A candidate securing the majority of votes is not automatically elected
options.b: The Supreme Court has no jurisdiction in any doubt or dispute arising in connection with the election of the President
options.c: The Presidential election cannot take place when one or more State Assemblies stand dissolved because all the State Assemblies form part of the electoral college
options.d: The total value of the votes allotted to both Houses of Parliament is much more than the total value of the votes of all the States taken together

explanation: Explanation: • The election of the President is governed by Article 54 and the Presidential and VicePresidential Elections Act, 1952. • The election uses proportional representation by means of single transferable vote, and voting is by secret ballot. • The value of votes of MPs is calculated by dividing the total value of votes of all elected MLAs by the number of elected MPs. • The combined value of votes of Parliament is indeed more than that of the States taken together. This ensures a federal balance tilted slightly towards the Union. • A candidate must secure a quota (total valid votes ÷ 2 + 1) to be elected. Merely securing a “majority” of first preference votes doesn’t guarantee automatic election if the quota isn’t met. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: The introduction of Pre-natal Diagnostic Techniques Bill in Parliament was prompted by the increasing incidence of

options.c: Spurious drugs being used for prenatal immunisation
options.d: Unqualified persons diagnosing pregnancy in villages by primitive methods

explanation: Explanation: • Amniocentesis and similar prenatal diagnostic techniques were widely misused in the 1980s to determine the sex of the foetus, followed by selective abortion of female foetuses. • This led to public outrage, activism, and debate across India. • Consequently, Parliament enacted the PreNatal Diagnostic Techniques (Regulation and Prevention of Misuse) Act in 1994, effective from 1996, later amended in 2003 to include pre-conception techniques. • The Act prohibits sex selection before or after conception and regulates diagnostic techniques to prevent misuse. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following is not in the State List under the Constitution of India?
explanation: Explanation: • The Seventh Schedule divides subjects into Union List (List I), State List (List II), and Concurrent List (List III). • State List includes subjects like public order, police, public health, agriculture, fisheries, markets, betting and gambling. • Insurance falls under the Union List, giving Parliament the exclusive power to legislate on it. • This arrangement ensures economic and financial subjects of national importance remain under Union control. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following correctly reflects the position of the Upper House of the State Legislature as compared to the position of the Upper House of the Parliament?

options.a: While one-third of the members of the Rajya Sabha retire every second year, one-fourth of the members of the Legislative Council retire every eighteen months
options.b: There is no provision for a joint sitting of the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council in the States for resolving deadlocks while there is such a provision in the case of the two Houses of Parliament
options.c: While no Bill other than a Money Bill can originate in the State Legislative Council, no Bill can originate in the Rajya Sabha
options.d: While Rajya Sabha has twelve nominated members, the State Legislative Council has none

explanation: Explanation: • Like the Rajya Sabha, the Legislative Council is a permanent body, not subject to dissolution. One-third of its members retire every two years. • Key difference: o There is no provision for joint sitting of the Legislative Assembly and Council to resolve a deadlock. o At the Centre, Article 108 provides for a joint sitting of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha to resolve differences on ordinary bills. • A bill rejected by the Assembly ends; the Council cannot override it. This shows the Council is weaker than the Rajya Sabha. Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: The Constitution of India borrowed the scheme of Indian Federation from the Constitution of
explanation: Explanation: • The Indian Constitution borrowed features from many constitutions: o British → Parliamentary system, Rule of law o US → Fundamental rights, judicial review o Irish → DPSPs, Presidential election method o Canadian → Federal scheme with a strong Centre, residuary powers with Union, Governor appointed by Centre, advisory jurisdiction of SC. • Article 1 describes India as a “Union of States”, indicating asymmetrical federalism like Canada — some states have special status. • Thus, India’s federal structure resembles Canada’s more than the USA’s. Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: A High Court can withdraw a case from a subordinate court and can deal with the case itself if it is satisfied that the case involves a substantial point of constitutional law. Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
explanation: Explanation: • Under Article 228, a High Court may withdraw a case from a subordinate court if: o It involves a substantial question of constitutional law. o The High Court may either dispose of the case itself or decide the constitutional question and send the case back. • The High Court’s decision on constitutional matters is binding on subordinate courts in its jurisdiction. • This provision ensures uniform interpretation of the Constitution within the state. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: The abolition of the I.A.S. and the I.P.S. has been recommended by the
explanation: Explanation: • The Rajamannar Committee was set up by the DMK Government of Tamil Nadu in 1969 under the chairmanship of Dr. P.V. Rajamannar. • Purpose: Examine Centre–State relations and recommend steps to make the federation more balanced. • The Committee submitted its report in 1971, making radical recommendations such as: o Abolition of All India Services (IAS, IPS, IFS), arguing they represented excessive central control over states. o Establishment of an Inter-State Council with real powers. o Curtailment of the Union’s power to dismiss State governments. • The IAS and IPS were retained, but this recommendation highlighted state-level discontent with central dominance. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: The only instance when the President of India exercised his power of veto related to
explanation: Explanation: • The President’s veto powers are of three types: o Absolute Veto – refusal to assent to the bill. o Suspensive Veto – returning a nonmoney bill for reconsideration. o Pocket Veto – taking no action. In 1954, President Dr. Rajendra Prasad used his absolute veto to withhold assent to the PEPSU (Patiala and East Punjab States Union) Appropriation Bill. • Reason: The bill was passed after President’s Rule ended, so it was no longer valid. • This is the only instance of the President using the absolute veto. Hence, option (b) is correct. •

subject: Indian Polity
question: The Chief Minister of a State in India is NOT eligible to vote in the Presidential election if

options.b: he is yet to prove his majority on the floor of the Lower House of the State legislature
options.c: he is a member of the Upper House of the State legislature
options.d: he is a care taker Chief Minister

explanation: Explanation: • Article 54: The Electoral College for Presidential elections consists of: o Elected members of both Houses of Parliament, and o Elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of States. • Members of Legislative Councils (Upper House) do not vote in Presidential elections. • Therefore, if the Chief Minister is a member of the Legislative Council, he is not part of the Electoral College, hence cannot vote. • Whether he is caretaker or has to prove majority has no effect on eligibility. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Among the four pairs given below, which one consists of a correct combination of dignitaries who became Vice-Presidents after having held diplomatic posts like Ambassadors and High Commissioners?

options.a: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan and G.S. Pathak
options.b: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan and V.V. Giri
options.c: Dr. Zakir Hussain and K.R. Narayanan

explanation: Explanation: • Dr. S. Radhakrishnan: o Served as India’s Ambassador to the USSR (1949–52). o Later became the first Vice-President (1952–62) and second President (1962–67). • V.V. Giri: o Served as High Commissioner to Ceylon (Sri Lanka) in 1947. o Became Vice-President in 1967 and later the fourth President of India (1969–74). • G.S. Pathak and B.D. Jatti were not diplomats before becoming Vice-President. • K.R. Narayanan was indeed a diplomat, but he became Vice-President much later; the correct pair as per the question is (b). Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following is in the Concurrent List in the Constitution of India?
explanation: Explanation: • Seventh Schedule – List III (Concurrent List) includes matters on which both Parliament and State Legislatures can legislate. • Population control and family planning is specifically listed in the Concurrent List. • Public health and sanitation → State List. • Capitation taxes and treasure trove → State List. • Central law prevails in case of conflict (Article 254), but States may also legislate. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following is a feature common to both the Indian Federation and the American Federation?

options.d: A federal Supreme Court to interpret the Constitution

explanation: Explanation: • Indian and American federations differ significantly: o India: Single citizenship, single integrated judiciary, three lists. o USA: Dual citizenship, dual judiciary, two lists (Federal & State). • Common feature: Existence of a federal Supreme Court to interpret the Constitution. o In India – Article 124 establishes the Supreme Court as guardian of the Constitution. o In the USA – SCOTUS plays a similar role. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Among the four political parties listed below, which one was the last to be formed?
explanation: Explanation: • Conservative Party (UK) – founded 1834. • Democratic Party (USA) – founded around 1828 (oldest active party). • Republican Party (USA) – founded 1854. • Indian National Congress – founded in 1885, during British rule. • It became the principal organization of the freedom movement and later dominant political party post-independence. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following comes under the jurisdiction of both the High Courts and the Supreme Court?

options.a: Disputes between the Centre and the States
options.b: Disputes between the States inter se
options.d: Protection against the violation of the Constitution

explanation: Explanation: • Article 32: Supreme Court’s power to issue writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights. • Article 226: High Courts have power to issue writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights and other legal rights. • Hence, jurisdiction over Fundamental Rights is concurrent between High Courts and Supreme Court. • Disputes between Centre and States or States inter se fall under original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court only (Article 131). Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the table given below providing some details of the results of the election to the Karnataka State Legislative Assembly held in December, 1994. Political Party Percentage of popular Number of votes obtained seats secured Janata Dal 36 116 Congress 31 35 BJP 20.4 40 In terms of electoral analysis, the voter-seat distortion is to be explained as the result of the adoption of the
explanation: Explanation: • India follows the First-Past-The-Post (FPTP) electoral system, also called the simple majority system. • Under this system, the candidate who secures the highest number of votes in a constituency wins, regardless of whether they have an absolute majority (>50%). • This often leads to voter-seat distortion, i.e., the proportion of seats won does not match the proportion of votes polled. • In the example, Janata Dal won 36% of votes but secured 116 seats, whereas Congress with 31% got only 35 seats, highlighting the distortion. • This is a known feature of FPTP — it favors larger parties in concentrated areas and can disadvantage dispersed vote bases. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following statements regarding ‘Exit Poll’ is correct?

options.a: ‘Exit Poll’ is a term used to denote a post-election survey of voters regarding the candidate in whose favour they had exercised their franchise
options.b: ‘Exit Poll’ and ‘Opinion Poll’ are one and the same
options.c: ‘Exit Poll’ is a device through which results of voting can be most exactly predicted
options.d: ‘Exit Poll’ is an administrative device made recently by the Chief Election Commissioner to prevent impersonation

explanation: Explanation: • Exit Poll refers to a post-election survey conducted immediately after voters have cast their votes, asking them whom they voted for. • It is different from Opinion Poll, which is conducted before the election, to gauge likely voting trends. • Exit polls attempt to predict the likely outcome of elections based on responses from voters leaving polling booths. • In India, the Election Commission regulates exit polls, and publishing their results during the election process is restricted to ensure fair elections. • They are not official results and can sometimes be inaccurate. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following is correct in respect of the commencement of the election process in India?

options.a: The recommendation for election is made by the government and the notification for election is issued by the Election Commission
options.b: The recommendation for election is made by the Election Commission and the notification for election is issued by the Home Ministry at the Centre and Home Departments in the States
options.c: The recommendation for election is made by the Election Commission and the notification for election is issued by the President and Governors of the States concerned
options.d: Both the exercises of making a recommendation for election and that of issuing a notification in respect of it are done by Election Commission

explanation: Explanation: • The election process begins with a notification calling upon constituencies to elect members. • Government recommends the holding of elections (usually after completion or premature dissolution of the House). • The Election Commission then issues notification to schedule the election programme. • For Lok Sabha elections, the President issues the formal notification, but based on the advice of the Election Commission, and similarly, the Governor issues it for State Assembly elections. • The Election Commission of India (ECI) plays a central role in scheduling, supervising, and conducting elections. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Who among the following have the right to vote in the elections to both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha?

options.a: Elected members of the Lower House of the Parliament
options.b: Elected members of the Upper House of the Parliament
options.c: Elected members of the Upper House of the State Legislature
options.d: Elected members of the Lower House of the State Legislature

explanation: Explanation: • Elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies (Vidhan Sabha) vote in: o Lok Sabha elections → As electors (citizens). o Rajya Sabha elections → As part of the electoral college, through single transferable vote. • Elected MPs (Lok Sabha) vote in Presidential elections but not in Rajya Sabha elections. • Upper House members (both Parliament & State Legislative Council) do not vote in Lok Sabha elections. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following States of India does not have a Legislative Council so far even though the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956 provides for it?
explanation: Explanation: • Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) exists in only a few states: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, and Jammu & Kashmir. • Madhya Pradesh, despite the constitutional provision, has never created a Legislative Council. • Article 169 enables creation/abolition of Councils but does not make them mandatory. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, etc. (Article 15 of the Constitution of India) is a Fundamental Right classifiable under

options.a: the Right to Freedom of Religion

explanation: Explanation: • Article 15 is part of Part III (Fundamental Rights) under the Right to Equality (Articles 14–18). • It prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth, ensuring equality before law and protection against arbitrary state actions. • It allows for special provisions for women, children, and socially & educationally backward classes. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: In which one of the following States of India it is legal for a Hindu male and illegal for a Muslim male to have more than one living wife?
explanation: Explanation: • Goa follows a common civil code based on the Portuguese Civil Code of 1867. • Under this code, polygamy is legal for Hindus under certain conditions, but Muslims cannot practice polygamy. • In the rest of India, Hindus are prohibited from bigamy/polygamy under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, but Muslim men are permitted up to four wives under personal law. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Agricultural income-tax is assigned to the State Governments by
explanation: Explanation: • Agricultural income is a State subject under List II (State List) of the Seventh Schedule. • Parliament cannot levy income tax on agricultural income; only state legislatures can. • This division is directly provided by the Constitution, not by any commission or council. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following is incorrect in respect of Local Government in India?

options.a: According to the Indian Constitution, local government is not an independent tier in the federal system
options.b: 30% of the seats in local bodies are reserved for women
options.c: Local government finances are to be provided by a Commission
options.d: Elections to local bodies are to be determined by a Commission

explanation: Explanation: • Local government in India is not a constitutionally independent federal tier; it functions under state control. • 73rd and 74th Amendments (1992) constitutionalised Panchayati Raj and Urban Local Bodies, providing for: o State Finance Commissions for financial devolution. o State Election Commissions for regular elections. o Reservation for women and weaker sections. • Still, they remain subordinate to state legislatures, not sovereign tiers. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: The power of the Supreme Court of India to decide disputes between the Centre and the States falls under its
explanation: Explanation: • The Supreme Court has three types of jurisdiction — original, appellate and advisory. • Its exclusive original jurisdiction (Article 131) extends to any dispute: • Between the Government of India and one or more States, • Between the Government of India and one or more States on one side and one or more States on the other, • Between two or more States, if the dispute involves a question of law or fact on which the existence or extent of a legal right depends. • In addition, Article 32 gives the Supreme Court original jurisdiction in the enforcement of Fundamental Rights. • The Court can also transfer cases between High Courts or withdraw cases involving substantial questions of law. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: When the Chief Justice of a High Court acts in an administrative capacity, he is subject to

options.a: the writ jurisdiction of any of the other judges of the High Court
options.b: special control exercised by the Chief Justice of India
options.c: discretionary powers of the Governor of the state
options.d: special powers provided to the Chief Minister in this regard

explanation: Explanation: • The Chief Justice of a High Court exercises both judicial and administrative powers. • When acting in an administrative capacity, his decisions are not immune from judicial review. • Such decisions can be challenged under the writ jurisdiction (Article 226) of any other judge of the same High Court. • Neither the Governor nor the Chief Minister has control in this regard, and the Chief Justice of India does not exercise direct supervisory power over High Court administration. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: According to the Constitution of India, the term ‘district judge’ shall not include

options.d: chief judge of a small cause court

explanation: Explanation: • Articles 233 to 237 in Part VI of the Constitution deal with the subordinate judiciary. • The expression ‘district judge’ includes: • Judge of a city civil court, • Additional district judge, • Joint district judge, • Assistant district judge, • Chief judge of a small cause court, • Chief presidency magistrate, additional chief presidency magistrate, • Sessions judge, additional sessions judge, assistant sessions judge. • Tribunal judges are not included in this definition. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: What is the system of governance in the Panchayati Raj setup?

options.a: Single-tier structure of local self-government at the village level
options.b: Two-tier system of local self-government at the village and block levels
options.c: Three-tier structure of local self-government, at the village, block and district levels
options.d: Four-tier system of local self-government at the village, block, district and state levels

explanation: Explanation: • The 73rd Amendment Act (1992) established a three-tier Panchayati Raj system throughout the country: 1. Village level – Gram Panchayat 2. Intermediate (block) level – Panchayat Samiti 3. District level – Zila Parishad • States with populations below 20 lakh may not have the intermediate level. • Members are directly elected at all levels, ensuring uniformity across states. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following statements is correct? The Prime Minister of India

options.a: is free to choose his ministers only from among those who are members of either House of the Parliament
options.b: can choose his cabinet colleagues after due counselling by the President of India in this regard
options.c: has full discretion in the choice of persons who are to serve as ministers in his cabinet
options.d: has only limited powers in the choice of his cabinet colleagues because of the discretionary power vested with the President of India

explanation: Explanation: • The Prime Minister is the real head of the Union executive. • He has full discretion in selecting ministers, allocating portfolios, reshuffling, and advising the President on appointments. • The President is bound by the Prime Minister’s advice and cannot exercise discretion in choosing ministers. • Even non-members of Parliament can be appointed ministers but must get elected within six months. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: B.R. Ambedkar was elected to the Constituent Assembly from
explanation: Explanation: • Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, though a resident of Bombay, was not elected from Bombay Presidency. • His supporters arranged for his election from a seat in West Bengal. • He later became Chairman of the Drafting Committee, playing a crucial role in shaping the Constitution. • He is known as the Father of the Indian Constitution. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Assertion (A): The word ‘minority’ is not defined in the Constitution of India. Reason (R): The Minorities Commission is not a constitutional body.

options.a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true but R is false
options.d: A is false but R is true

explanation: Explanation: • The Constitution does not define ‘minority’, but Articles 29–30 mention minorities based on language or religion. • The Minorities Commission was set up by an executive resolution in 1978, later made statutory by the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992. • It is not a constitutional body. • However, the fact that the Commission is not constitutional does not explain why ‘minority’ is undefined. Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following countries has more or less evolved a two-party system?
explanation: Explanation: • Bangladesh has evolved a two-party dominant system: • Awami League (AL) – secular, centre-left • Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) – centreright • Though smaller parties exist, national politics is dominated by AL and BNP, often heading coalitions. • Sri Lanka has a multiparty system; Pakistan has unstable multiparty politics; Myanmar has historically been under military or one-party rule. Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: In which of the following countries will the no confidence motion to bring down the government passed by the legislature be valid only when the legislature is able to find simultaneously a majority to elect a successor government?
explanation: Explanation: • Germany introduced the concept of Constructive Vote of No Confidence in its Basic Law (1949) to avoid the political instability experienced during the Weimar Republic. • Under this system, a motion of no confidence must simultaneously propose a successor Chancellor, who must secure an absolute majority in the Bundestag. • If the motion passes, the incumbent Chancellor is removed and the proposed successor automatically takes office. • This prevents opposition parties from merely destabilizing the government without having an alternative ready. • It discourages frequent government collapses, ensuring continuity and stability in the parliamentary system. • The system has been adopted by other nations like Spain, Hungary, Israel, Albania, Belgium etc. Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following was NOT proposed by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment in the area of Panchayati Raj?

options.a: Thirty per cent seats in all elected rural local bodies will be reserved for women candidates at all levels
options.b: The States will constitute their Finance Commissions to allocate resources to Panchayati Raj Institutions
options.c: The Panchayati Raj elected functionaries will be disqualified to hold their offices if they have more than two children
options.d: The elections will be held in six months time if Panchayati Raj bodies are superceded or dissolved by the State government

explanation: Explanation: • The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs). • It mandated reservation of not less than onethird (33⅓%) of the total seats and offices of chairpersons for women, not “thirty per cent”. • It required the State Finance Commission to be constituted every five years to recommend distribution of financial resources between the state and PRIs. • It mandated fresh elections within six months if a Panchayat is dissolved before completing its five-year term. • Some states introduced a two-child norm for PRI representatives, but this is not a constitutional provision. • The wording “thirty per cent” is factually incorrect — the actual figure is one-third, making option (a) wrong. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Proportional representation is NOT necessary in a country where

options.d: there is a fusion of Presidential and Parliamentary forms of governments

explanation: Explanation: • Proportional Representation (PR) is designed to reflect the share of votes in the share of seats, which is especially important in multiparty democracies. • In a two-party system, electoral outcomes under FPTP usually mirror the popular vote proportions, so PR adds little value. • PR is typically used where there are many parties, to prevent over-representation of dominant parties and under-representation of smaller ones. • Countries like USA and UK with two-party dominance (Democrats–Republicans, Labour– Conservatives) function well with simple majority systems. • PR in such countries would complicate the system without changing outcomes significantly. • The absence of PR in two-party systems does not lead to disproportionate results, unlike in fragmented systems. Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: State Funding of elections takes place in
explanation: Explanation: • State funding means financial support provided by the government to political parties or candidates, either partially or fully, to contest elections. • Germany and Austria have well-established systems of public funding for political parties and elections. • The aim is to reduce dependence on private donors, limit the influence of vested interests, and curb corruption. • In Germany, parties receive funds based on votes secured and donations received, ensuring a mix of public and private support. • The system helps promote transparency, fairness, and level playing fields for smaller parties. • Countries like the USA, UK, and Canada have either no public funding or very limited mechanisms, especially for political parties themselves. • Germany’s model is often cited as a balanced and stable approach to political finance reform. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: The concept of Public Interest Litigation originated in
explanation: Explanation: • Public Interest Litigation (PIL) originated in the United States during the 1960s–1970s as a means to promote public causes through judicial action. • It allowed individuals or groups not directly affected to approach courts for protecting public rights, such as environmental protection or civil liberties. • PIL was used extensively by civil rights groups, consumer bodies, and NGOs in the US to address systemic issues. • In India, PIL was introduced in the late 1970s, pioneered by Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer and Justice P.N. Bhagwati. • It became a powerful tool in the 1980s to make justice more accessible, particularly to poor and marginalized communities. • PIL led to judicial activism, enabling courts to address issues like bonded labour, prison reforms, environment, and rights of vulnerable groups. • Unlike in the US, Indian PIL has a broader scope and relaxed locus standi, making it unique in global jurisprudence. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: If the Prime Minister of India belonged to the Upper House of Parliament

options.a: he will not be able to vote in his favour in the event of a no-confidence motion
options.b: he will not be able to speak on the Budget in the Lower House
options.c: he can make statements only on the Upper House
options.d: he has to become a member of the Lower House within six months after being sworn-in as the Prime Minister

explanation: Explanation: • Under the Constitution, the Prime Minister can be a member of either House of Parliament — Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha. • No-confidence motions are exclusively moved and decided in the Lok Sabha, as it represents the directly elected House. • A Prime Minister who is a member of the Rajya Sabha can participate in debates in the Lok Sabha but cannot vote on the motion. • This reflects the principle that executive authority is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabh. • Several PMs — Indira Gandhi (1966) for a few months, H.D. Deve Gowda (1996), and Manmohan Singh (2004–14) — were members of the Rajya Sabha during their tenure. • This arrangement maintains flexibility while upholding parliamentary accountability. • He does not need to shift to Lok Sabha unless politically desired. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: In the Presidential election in India, every elected member of the Legislative Assembly of a State shall have as many votes… “population” here means the population as ascertained by the
explanation: Explanation: • The value of votes for MLAs is based on the 1971 Census population figures. • The 42nd Amendment (1976) froze seat allocation and population figures until 2001, later extended to 2026 by the 84th Amendment. • The freeze was intended to incentivize states for population control. • This ensures uniformity and stability in presidential elections. • The 1971 base continues to be used despite later censuses. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Assertion (A): The reservation of thirty-three per cent of seats for women in Parliament and State Legislatures does not require Constitutional amendment. Reason (R): Political parties contesting elections can allocate thirty-three per cent of seats they contest to women candidates without any Constitutional amendment.

options.a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not a correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

explanation: Explanation: • Reservation of seats in legislatures requires a constitutional amendment, like the 73rd and 74th Amendments did for Panchayats and Municipalities. • Political parties can voluntarily allot 33% of tickets to women without constitutional changes. • There is currently no constitutional provision reserving seats for women in Parliament or State Assemblies. • The 108th Amendment Bill (2008) proposed it but remains unpassed. • So A is false, R is true. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: In which one of the following countries are 75 per cent of seats in both Houses of Parliament filled on the basis of first-past-the-post system and 25 per cent on the basis of Proportional Representation • system of elections?
explanation: Explanation: • Germany follows a mixed-member electoral system. • Around half to three-fourths of seats are filled through FPTP (constituency) elections. • The remaining seats are allocated through Proportional Representation (party lists). • This ensures local representation plus overall proportionality in the Bundestag. • Parties must cross a 5% threshold or win 3 constituencies to qualify for PR allocation. Hence, option (a) is correct. This date marks the completion of Constitution-making and its formal enactment. • January 26 was chosen for its symbolic significance in the freedom struggle. Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: In the following quotation “WE, THE PEOPLE OF INDIA, having solemnly resolved to constitute India into a Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic and to secure to all its citizens: JUSTICE, social, economic and political; LIBERTY of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship; EQUALITY of status and of opportunity; and to promote among them all; FRATERNITY assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation; In our Constituent Assembly this ‘X’ do hereby adopt, enact and give to ourselves this Constitution.” … ‘X’ stands for
explanation: Explanation: • The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 by the Constituent Assembly. • It came into effect on 26 January 1950, commemorating Purna Swaraj Day (1930). • The adoption date is explicitly mentioned in the Preamble. Codes: ABCD (a) 3 4 1 2 (b) 4 2 3 1 (c) 3 2 1 4 (d) 4 3 2 1 Answer: (b) Explanation: • The President takes an oath to uphold the Constitution and the law (Art. 60). • Judges of the Supreme Court swear to faithfully discharge their duties (Art. 124). • Members of Parliament swear to bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution (Art. 99). • Union Ministers take two oaths — of office and of secrecy (Art. 75). • These oaths ensure accountability to the Constitution and democratic principles. Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: The Dinesh Goswami Committee recommended

options.a: the constitution of state-level election commissions
options.b: List System of election to the Lok Sabha
options.d: a ban on the candidature of independent candidates in the parliamentary elections

explanation: Explanation: • The Dinesh Goswami Committee (1990) was set up to suggest electoral reforms. • It recommended partial state funding of elections to reduce money power in politics. • Suggested reforms included limiting the number of constituencies, increasing security deposits, and introducing Electronic Voting Machines. • Proposed proxy voting for personnel posted abroad. • Recommended a Model Code of Conduct and speedy disposal of election disputes. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Assertion (A): Willful disobedience or noncompliance of Court Orders and use of derogatory language about judicial behaviour amounts to Contempt of Court. Reason (R): Judicial activism cannot be practised without arming the judiciary with punitive powers to punish contemptuous behaviour.

options.a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not a correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

explanation: Explanation: • Contempt of Court is defined under the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971. • Civil Contempt involves willful disobedience to court orders. • Criminal Contempt includes actions that scandalize the court, prejudice judicial proceedings, or obstruct justice. • Judicial activism relies on the authority and dignity of courts, which is protected by contempt powers (Art. 129 & 215). • R is true but it explains a broader principle, not exactly why A is true. Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following Schedules of the Constitution of India contains provisions regarding Anti-Defection Act?
explanation: Explanation: • The Tenth Schedule was inserted by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985. • It is popularly known as the Anti-Defection Law. • It lays down the grounds for disqualification of MPs and MLAs on the grounds of defection. • Disqualification applies if a member voluntarily gives up membership of the party or votes/abstains contrary to party direction without permission. • Exceptions include mergers and splits (though later the 91st Amendment removed recognition of splits). • The Presiding Officer (Speaker/Chairman) decides disqualification cases. • Judicial review of the Speaker’s decision was upheld in Kihoto Hollohan case (1992). Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: The Indian parliamentary system is different from the British parliamentary system in that India has

options.a: both a real and a nominal executive

explanation: Explanation: • Judicial review is a core feature of the Indian Constitution, allowing courts to strike down laws that violate the Constitution. • Articles 13, 32, 131–136, 226, 245–246 empower courts to review legislative, executive, and even judicial actions. • In Britain, Parliament is supreme — no court can declare a law unconstitutional. • India, like the USA, has a written Constitution, making judicial review essential to maintain constitutional supremacy. • This is a key distinction: the UK follows parliamentary sovereignty, while India follows constitutional supremacy. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: The Constitution of India recognises
explanation: Explanation: • The Constitution does not define “minority”, but refers to religious and linguistic minorities in various Articles. • Article 29(1): Protects the right to conserve distinct language, script or culture of any section of citizens. • Article 29(2): Prohibits denial of admission to educational institutions on grounds of religion, race, caste, language. • Article 30(1): Gives minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. • Article 30(2): Prohibits discrimination in granting aid to minority institutions. • Articles 347, 350A, 350B: Provide for linguistic protection, instruction in mother tongue, and appointment of a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities. • Sikh community’s right to wear and carry Kirpans is also recognized (Art. 25). Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: In the new Panchayati Raj Bill enacted in 1993, there are several fresh provisions deviating from the past. Which one of the following is not one such provision?

options.a: A number of added responsibilities in the area of agriculture, rural development, primary education and social forestry among others.
options.b: Elections being made mandatory for all posts at the time they are due.
options.c: A statutory representation for women in the panchayats, upto a third of the strength.
options.d: Regular remuneration to the panchayat members, so as to ensure their punctuality and accountability

explanation: Explanation: • The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 gave constitutional status to PRIs. • It introduced eleven functional areas including agriculture, rural development, primary education, social forestry, etc. • Made regular elections compulsory even if bodies are dissolved — within six months. • Provided reservation of not less than onethird seats for women in all Panchayati Raj bodies. • There is no constitutional mandate for regular remuneration to panchayat members. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following statements: An amendment of the Constitution of India can be initiated by the (1) Lok Sabha (2) Rajya Sabha (3) State Legislatures (4) President Which of the above statements is/are correct?
explanation: Explanation: • Article 368 lays down the procedure for amending the Constitution. • An amendment bill can be introduced in either House of Parliament — Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha. • It cannot be initiated by State Legislatures or the President. • The bill must be passed in each House by a special majority: o Majority of total membership, and o Two-thirds majority of members present and voting. • For federal provisions, ratification by half of State Legislatures is also required. • The President must give assent once passed; he cannot withhold or return it. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following statements regarding the National Human Rights Commission of India: (1) Its Chairman must be a retired Chief Justice of India. (2) It has formations in each state as State Human Rights Commission. (3) Its powers are only recommendatory in nature. (4) It is mandatory to appoint a woman as a member of the Commission.
explanation: Explanation: • The NHRC was established in 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 (not constitutional). • Its Chairman must be a retired Chief Justice of India. • States may set up State Human Rights Commissions, but they are not formations of NHRC; they are separate statutory bodies. • NHRC’s powers are recommendatory, not binding — it can inquire and recommend but not punish. • There is no mandatory requirement to appoint a woman member. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: A British citizen staying in India cannot claim Right to

options.c: Protection of life and personal liberty

explanation: Explanation: Fundamental Rights only for citizens include: • Protection from discrimination (Art. 15), • Equality of opportunity in public employment (Art. 16), • Freedom of speech, assembly, association, movement, residence, profession (Art. 19), • Cultural & educational rights of minorities (Art. 30). • Rights available to all (citizens & foreigners) include: • Equality before law (Art. 14), • Protection of life & liberty (Art. 21), • Freedom of religion (Art. 25), • Rights against exploitation (Art. 23–24), etc. • Hence, a British citizen in India cannot claim Art. 19 rights, including freedom of trade/profession. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: “….instil into the vast millions of workers, men and women, who actually do the job, a sense of partnership and of cooperative performance....” The above passage relates to
explanation: Explanation: • Launched on 2 Oct 1952, the Community Development Programme (CDP) sought people’s participation in rural development. • Implemented via Community Development Blocks (~100 villages, 400–500 sq km, 60–70k population). • Emphasised self-help, cooperation, and local initiative rather than top-down delivery. • Covered multiple sectors: agriculture, irrigation, health, education, roads, sanitation. • Provided the administrative framework that later supported Panchayati Raj expansion in the 1960s. Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: The Speaker can ask a member of the House to stop speaking and let another member speak. This phenomenon is known as
explanation: Explanation: • “Yielding the floor”: the Chair/Speaker directs a member to give way so another may speak. • Ensures orderly debate, time discipline, and balanced participation among parties. • Rule of Chair’s authority: members must resume their seats when Speaker rises. • Different from interpellation (formal question to govt) and crossing the floor (changing seating sides). Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following statements about the Attorney-General of India: 1. He is appointed by the President of India. 2. He must have the same qualifications as are required for a Judge of the Supreme Court. 3. He must be a member of either House of Parliament. 4. He can be removed by impeachment by Parliament. Which of these statements are correct?
explanation: Explanation: • Art. 76: Appointed by the President; tenure at President’s pleasure (no fixed term). • Qualifications: eligible to be SC Judge (citizen + 5 yrs HC judge/10 yrs HC advocate/distinguished jurist). • Not required to be an MP; may participate but not vote in Parliament/committees. • No impeachment: removal is executive pleasure, not a legislative process. • Has right of audience in all courts and advises Union Govt/President on legal matters. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following functionaries: 1. Cabinet Secretary 2. Chief Election Commissioner 3. Union Cabinet Ministers 4. Chief Justice of India. Their correct sequence, in the Order of Precedence, is
explanation: Explanation: • Order of Precedence (protocol list): CJI ranks above Union Cabinet Ministers (by seniority), followed by CEC, then Cabinet Secretary. • It is ceremonial, used for state functions, not a line of succession or power hierarchy. • Reflects constitutional importance and protocol seating/priority at official events. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: The primary function of the Finance Commission in India is to

options.a: distribute revenue between the Centre and the States
options.c: advise the President on financial matters
options.d: allocate funds to various ministries of the Union and State Governments

explanation: Explanation: • Art. 280: Constituted every 5 years (or earlier) to recommend tax devolution Union→States and among States (vertical & horizontal). • Recommends grants-in-aid under Art. 275, fiscal equalization, and other referred matters (e.g., disaster relief norms). • Submits report to President; action taken tabled in Parliament. • Does not prepare the Union Budget or allocate to ministries (that’s MoF/Parliament). Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: The State which has the largest number of seats reserved for the Scheduled Tribes in Lok Sabha is
explanation: Explanation: • Arts. 330–332: Reservation for SC/ST seats proportional to population. • As per the then delimitation: Madhya Pradesh had the highest ST-reserved seats among listed options (e.g., ~5), Gujarat ~4, Bihar/UP—none. • Subject to periodic readjustment post-census, but then-current data favoured M.P. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: A college student desires to get elected to the Municipal Council of his city. The validity of his nomination would depend on the important condition, among others, that

options.a: he obtains permission from the Principal of his college
options.b: he is a member of a political party
options.c: his name figures in the Voters’ List
options.d: he files a declaration owing allegiance to the Constitution of India

explanation: Explanation: • Urban local body eligibility includes: citizenship, age ≥21, name on electoral roll of the concerned ward, and no disqualification. • Party membership/college permission are not legal prerequisites. • Reservation norms (SC/ST/OBC/Women) may apply by seat; otherwise no separate allegiance declaration needed beyond the nomination affidavit. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: The Parliament can make any law for the whole or any part of India for implementing International treaties

options.a: with the consent of all the States
options.b: with the consent of the majority of States
options.c: with the consent of the States concerned
options.d: without the consent of any State

explanation: Explanation: • Art. 253: Parliament may legislate for whole/any part of India to implement international treaties, agreements, conventions, even on State List subjects. • State consent not required; ensures India can fulfil international obligations. • Examples: UN Privileges & Immunities Act, 1947, Geneva Conventions Act, 1960, AntiHijacking Act, 1982. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following statements about a Money Bill is not correct?

options.a: A Money Bill can be tabled in either House of Parliament
options.b: The Speaker of Lok Sabha is the final authority to decide whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not
options.c: The Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill passed by Lok Sabha and send it for consideration within 14 days
options.d: The President cannot return a Money Bill to Lok Sabha for reconsideration

explanation: Explanation: • Art. 110: A Money Bill can be introduced only in Lok Sabha, and only with President’s recommendation. • Speaker’s certification is final and cannot be questioned in court (as a rule of internal procedure). • Rajya Sabha can recommend amendments but must return within 14 days; Lok Sabha may accept/reject. • President cannot return a Money Bill; can only assent or withhold. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: The 73rd Constitution Amendment Act, 1992 refers to the

options.a: generation of gainful employment in rural areas
options.c: laying the foundation for strong and vibrant Panchayati Raj Institutions in the country
options.d: guarantee of right to life, liberty, equality and security

explanation: Explanation: • Inserted Part IX (Arts. 243–243-O) and Eleventh Schedule (29 subjects). • Provided 3-tier PRIs, regular elections, State Election Commissions, State Finance Commissions. • Reservations: ≥1/3 seats & chairpersons for women; SC/ST as per population. • Objective: devolution, democratic decentralization, local planning & implementation. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?

options.b: Diu is an island in the Gulf of Khambhat
options.c: Daman and Diu were separated from Goa by the 56th Amendment of the Constitution of India
options.d: Dadra and Nagar Haveli were under French colonial rule till 1954

explanation: Explanation: • Goa statehood on 30 May 1987 (correct). • Diu is an island off the Gulf of Khambhat (correct). • 56th Amendment, 1987: granted Goa statehood; Daman & Diu remained a UT (correct). • Dadra & Nagar Haveli were Portuguese (not French); liberated 1954, integrated 1961 (so (d) is incorrect). Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: In what way does the Indian Parliament exercise control over the administration?

options.a: Through Consultative Committees of various ministries
options.c: By making the administrators send periodic reports
options.d: By compelling the executive to issue writs

explanation: Explanation: • Parliament in India exercises executive accountability primarily through Parliamentary Committees because House time is limited and detailed examination of every policy or budget is not feasible in the main chamber. • Standing Committees (e.g., Public Accounts Committee (PAC), Estimates Committee, Public Undertakings Committee, DRSCs) and Ad hoc Committees are constituted for detailed scrutiny of administrative actions. • These Committees examine government policies, budgetary allocations, performance, policy implementation, and outcomes. • They can summon officials, demand documents, take evidence, and submit recommendations. This ensures continuous and informed oversight. • Consultative Committees attached to ministries are only advisory in nature, and do not have oversight powers. • Issuing writs is a judicial function, not a parliamentary one. • Parliament’s role is political and procedural, focusing on ensuring that the executive remains answerable for its decisions

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following statements regarding the High Courts in India: 1. There are eighteen High Courts in the country. 2. Three of them have jurisdiction over more than one State. 3. No Union Territory has a High Court of its own. 4. Judges of the High Court hold office till the age of 62. Which of these statements is/are correct?
explanation: Explanation: • Article 217 of the Constitution specifies that High Court Judges hold office until 62 years of age. • The number of High Courts has increased beyond 18 due to new States and UT reorganisations (e.g., Telangana High Court in 2019). So statement 1 . • Some High Courts have jurisdiction over more than one State/UT, e.g.: o Bombay High Court → Maharashtra, Goa, and UTs of Daman & Diu and Dadra & Nagar Haveli. o Punjab & Haryana High Court → jurisdiction over both states and Chandigarh. o Guwahati High Court → earlier had multiple North-Eastern states. Statement 2 is factually correct, but the answer framing focuses on elimination logic. • Delhi, a Union Territory, has its own High Court since 1966. Statement 3 . Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: If a new State of the Indian Union is to be created, which one of the following Schedules of the Constitution must be amended?
explanation: Explanation: • The First Schedule lists the names of States and Union Territories, along with their territorial extent. • When a new State is created, merged, or boundaries are altered, Parliament must amend the First Schedule under Articles 2 & 3. • This is done by a simple majority, not a special majority (as it is not treated as a constitutional amendment under Article 368). • Second Schedule deals with salaries and allowances of officials. • Third Schedule relates to forms of oaths and affirmations. • Fifth Schedule deals with administration of Scheduled Areas and Tribes. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which Article of the Constitution provides that it shall be the endeavour of every State to provide adequate facility for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage of education?
explanation: Explanation: • Article 350A was inserted by the Seventh Amendment (1956). • It places a directive obligation on States to endeavour to provide mother tongue instruction at the primary stage for children belonging to linguistic minorities. • The President may issue directions to ensure compliance with this Article. • Article 350 ensures citizens can submit representations to authorities in any language used in the Union or State. • Article 349 deals with special procedure regarding language (restriction on Parliament’s power to make language-related laws for 15 years). • Article 351 provides for promotion of Hindi as a national language. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: The Supreme Court of India tenders advice to the President on a matter of law or fact

options.b: only if he seeks such advice
options.c: only if the matter relates to the Fundamental Rights of citizens
options.d: only if the issue poses a threat to the unity and integrity of the country

explanation: Explanation: • Article 143 empowers the President to refer questions of law or fact to the Supreme Court for advisory opinion. • The Supreme Court cannot give advice suo motu (on its own). The President must initiate the reference. • The advisory jurisdiction is very wide — it is not limited to Fundamental Rights or national integrity issues. • Although the Court’s opinion is not binding, it carries great persuasive value. Examples include references on the Ayodhya dispute (1993) and Kerala Education Bill (1958). Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following duties is NOT performed by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?

options.a: To audit and report on all expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India
options.b: To audit and report on all expenditure from the Contingency Funds and Public Accounts
options.c: To audit and report on all trading, manufacturing, profit and loss accounts
options.d: To control the receipt and issue of public money, and to ensure that the public revenue is lodged in the exchequer

explanation: Explanation: • CAG (Articles 148–151) is an independent constitutional authority. • He audits: o Consolidated Fund of Union & States. o Contingency Funds and Public Accounts. o Departmental commercial undertakings and PSUs (as per law). • The CAG’s function is post-facto audit → he checks whether money was legally spent for the intended purpose. • Control over receipts and expenditure is exercised by the executive/treasury, not CAG. • This separation ensures checks and balances between executive financial control and independent audit. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the Fourth Schedule of the Constitution of India?

options.a: It lists the distribution of power between the Union and the States
options.b: It contains the languages listed in the Constitution
options.c: It contains the provisions regarding the administration of tribal areas
options.d: It allocates seats in the Council of States

explanation: Explanation: • The Fourth Schedule deals with allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) to States and Union Territories. • It ensures federal representation in the Upper House based on population while maintaining equality of status among States. • Seventh Schedule → Union, State, Concurrent Lists. • Eighth Schedule → Official languages. Fifth and Sixth Schedules → administration of Scheduled Areas and Tribes in different regions. Hence, option (d) is correct. • symbol reservation across states, and consultation rights with the ECI. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following statements regarding the political parties in India: 1. The Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides for the registration of political parties. 2. Registration of political parties is carried out by the Election Commission. 3. A national level political party is one which is recognised in four or more States. 4. During the 1999 general elections, there were six National and 48 State level parties recognised by the Election Commission. Which of these statements are correct?
explanation: Explanation: • Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 enables political parties to register with the Election Commission of India (ECI). • The ECI registers parties and recognises them as national or state parties under the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968. • A National Party must be recognised in four or more States and fulfill vote share or seat criteria (e.g., 6% valid votes + 4 Lok Sabha seats or recognition in 4 states). • In the 1999 General Elections, there were 6 National Parties and 48 State Parties, per ECI records. • Registration gives parties certain legal benefits, tax exemptions, and symbol reservation rights, while recognition gives them election privileges like free airtime,

subject: Indian Polity
question: The members of the Constituent Assembly which drafted the Constitution of India were

options.c: elected by the Legislative Assemblies of various provinces
options.d: elected by the Indian National Congress and Muslim League

explanation: Explanation: • The Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946 laid down the procedure for setting up a Constituent Assembly in India. • The Provincial Legislative Assemblies (elected under the 1935 Act in 1946 elections) were to elect members to the Assembly by the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote (STV). • Seats were allocated in proportion to population: 292 from provinces, 93 from princely states, and 4 from Chief Commissioner’s provinces, totaling 389 members. • The princely states nominated their representatives. There was no direct election by the people, and neither the British Parliament nor the Governor-General nominated all members. • After partition, the Assembly was reconstituted with 299 members, who drafted the Constitution over 2 years, 11 months, 18 days. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following rights was described by Dr B R Ambedkar as the heart and soul of the Constitution?
explanation: Explanation: • Article 32 guarantees the Right to Constitutional Remedies, i.e., the right to approach the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights. • The Supreme Court may issue five writs: o Habeas corpus (produce the body) o Mandamus (we command) o Prohibition (stop proceedings) o Certiorari (transfer/review of proceedings) o Quo warranto (by what authority) • Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called Article 32 the “heart and soul of the Constitution” because it gives teeth to Fundamental Rights, making them meaningful and enforceable. • It is itself a Fundamental Right, unique among constitutions. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following Articles of the Directive Principles of State Policy deals with the promotion of international peace and security?
explanation: Explanation: • Article 51 (Directive Principles, Part IV) directs the State to: o Promote international peace and security, o Maintain just and honourable relations between nations, o Foster respect for international law and treaty obligations, and o Encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration. • Article 51 reflects India’s commitment to world peace, aligning with Panchsheel principles and the UN Charter. • Article 48A: protection and improvement of the environment. • Article 43A: workers’ participation in management of industries. • Article 41: right to work, education, and public assistance. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: With reference to Indian Polity, which one of the following statements is correct?

options.a: Planning Commission is accountable to Parliament
options.b: President can make ordinance only when either of the two Houses of Parliament is not in session
options.c: The minimum age prescribed for appointment as a Judge of the Supreme Court is 40 years
options.d: National Development Council is constituted of Union Finance Minister and the Chief Ministers of all the States

explanation: Explanation: • Article 123 empowers the President to promulgate ordinances when either House of Parliament is not in session, and immediate action is necessary. • The ordinance has the same force as a law, but must be laid before Parliament and ceases to operate after six weeks of reassembly if not approved. • The Planning Commission (1950–2014) was an extra-constitutional advisory body, not accountable to Parliament. • There is no minimum age for Supreme Court Judges in Article 124; eligibility is based on 5 years as High Court judge, 10 years as High Court advocate, or eminent jurist. • National Development Council (NDC) included the PM (Chairman), Union Cabinet Ministers, Chief Ministers of all States, and UT representatives—not just the FM and CMs. Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following authorities recommends the principles governing the grants-inaid of the revenues to the states out of the Consolidated Fund of India?
explanation: Explanation: • Article 280 provides for a Finance Commission every five years to recommend: o Distribution of tax proceeds between Centre and States, o Principles for grants-in-aid of States’ revenues from the Consolidated Fund of India (Article 275), o Measures to augment State finances to support Panchayats and Municipalities (after 73rd and 74th Amendments). • Inter-State Council (Art. 263) is a coordination forum, not fiscal. • Union Finance Ministry executes finances but does not constitutionally recommend principles. • Public Accounts Committee scrutinises expenditure after it occurs. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: In the Indian Constitution, the Right to Equality is granted by Five Articles. They are
explanation: Explanation: • Articles 14 to 18 (Part III) guarantee Right to Equality: o Article 14: Equality before law and equal protection of laws (based on Dicey’s concept). o Article 15: Prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth; allows protective discrimination for women, children, SC/ST, and SEBC. o Article 16: Equal opportunity in matters of public employment; allows reservations. o Article 17: Abolition of untouchability and its practice in any form. o Article 18: Abolition of titles, except military and academic distinctions. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following amendments to the Indian Constitution empowers the President to send back any matter for reconsideration by the Council of Ministers?
explanation: Explanation: • 42nd Amendment (1976) made the President bound to act on the advice of the Council of Ministers. • 44th Amendment (1978) modified Article 74 to allow the President to once return the advice for reconsideration. • If the Council of Ministers reiterates its advice, the President must act on it. • This provision strengthens the President’s position slightly, enabling deliberation without disturbing parliamentary democracy. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: In the case of election to the Lok Sabha, the amount of Security deposited for general category candidates and SC/ST category candidates respectively is
explanation: Explanation: • Under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, candidates contesting Lok Sabha elections must deposit: o ₹10,000 for General category, o ₹5,000 for SC/ST candidates. • The deposit is forfeited if the candidate fails to secure more than 1/6th (16.67%) of valid votes polled in the constituency. • This provision aims to discourage non-serious candidates. Hence, option (c) is correct. (b) free and compulsory education for all children between the age of 6 and 14 years (c) reservation of 30 per cent posts for women in government recruitments (d) allocation of more number of parliamentary seats for recently created States Answer: (b) Explanation: • The 93rd Constitutional Amendment Bill (2001) inserted Article 21-A, making free and compulsory education for children aged 6–14 years a Fundamental Right. • It was later enacted as the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002. • The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act (RTE), 2009 operationalized it from 1 April

subject: Indian Polity
question: The term of the Lok Sabha

options.a: cannot be extended under any circumstances
options.b: can be extended by six months at a time
options.c: can be extended by one year at a time during the proclamation of emergency
options.d: can be extended for two years at a time during the proclamation of emergency

explanation: Explanation: • Article 83(2): Normal term of the Lok Sabha is 5 years from its first sitting. • During a National Emergency (Article 352), Parliament can extend the term of the Lok Sabha by one year at a time, and not beyond 6 months after the Emergency ends. • This was done during the Emergency (1975– 77). Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following statements is correct?

options.a: Only the Rajya Sabha and not the Lok Sabha can have nominated members
options.b: There is a constitutional provision for nominating two members belonging to the Anglo-Indian community to the Rajya Sabha
options.c: There is no constitutional bar for a nominated member to be appointed as a Union minister.
options.d: A nominated member can vote both in the Presidential and Vice-Presidential elections

explanation: Explanation: • Article 75 does not bar a nominated MP from being appointed as a Union Minister. Any MP—elected or nominated—can be appointed to the Council of Ministers. • Lok Sabha: Article 331 allowed the President to nominate up to two Anglo-Indians if not adequately represented. (This provision was abolished by the 104th Amendment Act, 2019). • Rajya Sabha: Article 80(1)(a) allows the President to nominate 12 members with special knowledge in literature, science, art or social service. There was no Anglo-Indian quota here. • Nominated MPs: o Cannot vote in Presidential elections (Article 54 explanation). o Can vote in Vice-Presidential elections (Article 66). Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Who has the power to enlarge the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India?

options.d: The Union Ministry of Law, Justice and Company Affairs

explanation: Explanation: • Article 138(1): Parliament may by law confer further jurisdiction and powers on the Supreme Court with respect to any matter in the Union List. • Article 138(2): Parliament may by law enable the Government of India and a State Government to refer disputes to the Supreme Court for advisory/jurisdictional settlement. • The President has advisory powers under Article 143, but cannot enlarge jurisdiction unilaterally. • CJI or Law Ministry have no such constitutional authority. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following High Courts has the territorial jurisdiction over Andaman and Nicobar Islands?
explanation: Explanation: • Calcutta High Court, established in 1862, has territorial jurisdiction over the State of West Bengal and the Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands. • This jurisdiction was conferred to facilitate administrative convenience during the colonial period and continues postindependence. • Madras HC covers Tamil Nadu & Puducherry; Andhra HC covers Andhra Pradesh; Orissa HC covers Odisha only. Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following Schedules of the Indian Constitution lists the names of States and specifies their territories?
explanation: Explanation: • First Schedule lists the names of States and Union Territories, and specifies their territorial extent. • Any creation, merger, or boundary change of States under Articles 2 & 3 requires amendment of the First Schedule through an ordinary law. • Second Schedule → Salaries, emoluments of constitutional authorities. • Third Schedule → Forms of oaths and affirmations. • Fourth Schedule → Allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: The Ninth Schedule to the Indian Constitution was added by:
explanation: Explanation: • First Amendment Act, 1951 inserted Article 31B and the Ninth Schedule. • Purpose: to protect land reform and agrarian legislation from being challenged in courts on the ground of violating Fundamental Rights, especially right to property. • Article 31B provides that none of the Acts included in the Ninth Schedule shall be deemed void for being inconsistent with Part III. • After Kesavananda Bharati (1973), laws inserted into the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 are open to judicial review if they violate the basic structure of the Constitution (I.R. Coelho case, 2007). Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: The second joint sitting of the two Houses of Indian Parliament was held to pass the Banking Service Commission (Repeal) Bill. Which of these statements is/are correct?
explanation: Explanation: • Article 108 allows joint sittings of both Houses in case of deadlock over an ordinary bill, not Money/CA bills. • There have been only three joint sittings in history: 1. Dowry Prohibition Bill (1961) – First joint sitting. 2. Banking Service Commission (Repeal) Bill (1978) – Second joint sitting. 3. Prevention of Terrorism Bill (POTA) (2002) – Third joint sitting. • All statements referring to these instances are correct. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution did the President give his assent to the ordinance on electoral reforms when it was sent back to him by the Union Cabinet without making any changes (in 2002)?
explanation: Explanation: • Article 123 empowers the President to promulgate ordinances when Parliament is not in session and immediate action is required. • An ordinance has the same force as an Act, but must be laid before Parliament and approved within 6 weeks of reassembly. • In 2002, the President returned the Electoral Reforms Ordinance for reconsideration. The Cabinet sent it back unchanged, and the President was constitutionally bound to promulgate it. • Articles 121 & 122 deal with Parliamentary proceedings, not ordinances; 124 deals with SC judges. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides that “It shall be the duty of the Union to protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance”?
explanation: Explanation: • Article 355: It is the duty of the Union to protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance, and to ensure that the Government of every State is carried on in accordance with the Constitution. • This Article forms the constitutional basis for Central intervention, including President’s Rule under Article 356 in grave situations. • It also provides the foundation for deployment of central forces to aid states. • Articles 215, 275, 325 deal with HCs, grants, and elections respectively. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following Bills must be passed by each House of the Indian Parliament separately, by special majority?
explanation: Explanation: • Article 368 lays down the procedure for Constitutional Amendment Bills. • They must be passed in each House separately by a special majority: o Majority of the total membership of the House, and o 2/3 of the members present and voting. • There is no provision for a joint sitting for Constitution Amendment Bills. • Certain amendments (e.g., affecting federal provisions like Articles 54, 73, 162) also require ratification by ½ of the State Legislatures. • Money Bills (Article 110) can only be introduced in Lok Sabha, and Rajya Sabha has limited powers. • Finance Bill includes financial provisions but follows ordinary or money bill procedures depending on type. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: With reference to Indian Public Finance, consider the following statements: 1. Disbursements from Public Accounts of India are subject to the Vote of Parliament. 2.
