The Indian Constitution provides for the establishment of a Consolidated Fund, a Public Account and a Contingency Fund for each State. 3. Appropriations and disbursements under the Railway Budget are subject to the same form of parliamentary control as other appropriations and disbursements. Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Explanation: • Public Account (Art. 266(2)) includes transactions like provident funds, small savings, etc. Parliamentary vote is not required for withdrawals from this account. • Constitution provides three funds — Consolidated Fund, Public Account, and Contingency Fund — separately for Union and each State. • Railway Budget is presented separately but receipts and expenditures are part of the Consolidated Fund. • Parliamentary control over Railway Budget appropriations is the same as General Budget, ensuring accountability. • Statement 1 is incorrect (no vote for Public Account), 2 and 3 are correct. Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following statements: 1. The highest criminal court of the district is the Court of District and Sessions Judge. 2. The District Judges are appointed by the Governor in consultation with the High Courts. 3. A person to be eligible for appointment as a District Judge should be an advocate or a pleader of seven years standing or more, or an officer in judicial service of the Union or the State. 4. When the Sessions Judge awards death sentence, it must be confirmed by the High Court before it is carried out. Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Explanation: • District & Sessions Judge is the highest civil and criminal judicial authority at the district level. • Appointment is made by the Governor in consultation with the High Court, ensuring judicial independence. • Eligibility: must be an advocate or pleader with 7+ years’ standing or a judicial officer in service. • Death sentences awarded by Sessions Judge require confirmation by the High Court even without appeal. • All four statements reflect the structure of district judiciary under the Constitution & CPC/CrPC. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Speaker of Lok Sabha has the power to adjourn the House sine die but, on prorogation, it is only the President who can summon the House. 2. Unless sooner dissolved or there is an extension of the term, there is an automatic dissolution of the Lok Sabha by efflux of time, at the end of the period of five years, even if no formal order of dissolution is issued by the President. 3. The Speaker of Lok Sabha continues in office even after the dissolution of the House and until ‘immediately before the first meeting of the House’. Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Explanation: • Adjournment sine die = ending a sitting indefinitely; this power lies with the Speaker. • Prorogation ends a session, and President has the power to summon or prorogue the House under Article 85. • Automatic dissolution occurs after 5 years, even without a formal order, unless extended during emergency. • Speaker remains in office till just before the first sitting of the new Lok Sabha — ensures continuity. • All three statements correctly reflect parliamentary procedure and constitutional practice. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following statements is not correct?

options.a: In Lok Sabha, a no-confidence motion has to set out the grounds on which it is based
options.b: In the case of a no-confidence motion in Lok Sabha, no conditions of admissibility have been laid down in the Rules
options.c: A motion of no-confidence, once admitted, has to be taken up within ten days of the leave being granted
options.d: Rajya Sabha is not empowered to entertain a motion of no-confidence

explanation: Explanation: • • • • • No-confidence motion (Rule 198, Lok Sabha Rules) expresses lack of confidence in the Council of Ministers as a whole. No grounds are required to be mentioned; even if mentioned, they do not form part of the motion. If 50 or more members support the motion, the Speaker admits it, and it must be taken up within 10 days. Rajya Sabha cannot move or pass noconfidence motions, as executive is responsible only to Lok Sabha. Statement (a) is factually incorrect, hence the correct answer. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following tasks: 1. Superintendence, direction and conduct of free and fair elections. 2. Preparation of electoral rolls for all elections to the Parliament, State Legislatures and the Office of the President and the Vice-President. 3. Giving recognition to political parties and allotting election symbols to political parties and individuals contesting the election. 4. Proclamation of final verdict in the case of election disputes. Which of the above are the functions of the Election Commission of India?
explanation: Explanation: • Article 324 vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission of India. • Functions include conduct of elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, President, Vice-President. • It prepares electoral rolls, recognises political parties, and allots symbols. • Election disputes are decided by courts, not the Election Commission. • So, 1, 2, and 3 are functions; 4 is not. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: The resolution for removing the Vice-President of India can be moved in the:
explanation: Explanation: • Article 67(b) provides for removal of the VicePresident by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha, passed by effective majority. • Lok Sabha must agree by simple majority, but the motion originates only in Rajya Sabha. • 14 days’ advance notice must be given for such a resolution. • There is no impeachment procedure, unlike for the President. • Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha discharges functions in case of vacancy. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: With reference to the Constitution of India, which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?

options.c: Post Office Savings Bank — Union List

explanation: Explanation: • Seventh Schedule distributes powers between Union, State, and Concurrent Lists. • Stock Exchanges and Futures Markets are mentioned in Union List – Entry 48, not in the State List. • Forests were transferred from State List to Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment, 1976. • Public Health is under the State List, Entry 6. • Post Office Savings Bank is under Union List, Entry 39. • Hence, the mismatch is in (b). Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following statements: 1. The highest deciding body for planning in India is the Planning Commission of India. 2. The Secretary of the Planning Commission of India is also the Secretary of National Development Council. 3. The Constitution includes economic and social planning in the Concurrent List in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Explanation: • National Development Council (NDC), set up in 1952, is the highest policy-making body on planning (apart from Parliament), not the Planning Commission. • Secretary of Planning Commission also acts as Secretary of the NDC, ensuring coordination. • Economic and Social Planning is listed in Concurrent List – Item 20. • Planning Commission (1950–2014) was executive & advisory, not constitutional. • NITI Aayog has replaced the Planning Commission since 2015. Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: With reference to Indian Parliament, which one of the following is not correct?

options.a: The Appropriation Bill must be passed by both the Houses of Parliament before it can be enacted into law
options.b: No money shall be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India except under the appropriation made by the Appropriation Act
options.c: Finance Bill is required for proposing new taxes but no other Bill/Act is required for making changes in the rates of taxes which are already under operation
options.d: No Money Bill can be introduced except on the recommendation of the President

explanation: Explanation: • • • • • • Finance Bill is required for proposing new taxes and also for changes in existing tax rates. Appropriation Bill authorises withdrawal from Consolidated Fund of India; must pass both Houses. Article 265: no tax can be levied or collected except by authority of law. Article 110 & Rules of Procedure govern Finance Bills, which must be enacted within 75 days. President’s recommendation is mandatory for introduction of Money Bills. (c) is factually incorrect, hence the answer. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following Articles of the Constitution of India says that the executive power of every State shall be so exercised as not to impede or prejudice the exercise of the executive power of the Union?
explanation: Explanation: • Article 257: The executive power of every State shall be exercised not to impede or prejudice the exercise of the executive power of the Union. • It allows the Union to give directions to States for ensuring smooth functioning. • It covers construction & maintenance of means of communication, protection of railways, and other matters of national importance. • Article 258 deals with delegation of Union functions to States. • Articles 355 and 356 relate to Union’s duty to protect States and President’s Rule. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following Articles of the Constitution of India prohibits the employment of children in factories?
explanation: Explanation: • Article 24: Prohibits employment of children below 14 years in factories, mines, or any hazardous employment. • It is part of the Fundamental Rights (Article 12–35), making it enforceable by law. • Violation attracts penal provisions under the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986. • Article 45 relates to free and compulsory education, Article 330 to reservation of seats, Article 368 to constitutional amendments. • This provision ensures protection of children and aligns with Directive Principles and international conventions. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: According to the National Human Rights Commission Act, 1993, who amongst the following can be its Chairman?

options.a: Any serving Judge of the Supreme Court
options.b: Any serving Judge of the High Court
options.c: Only a retired Chief Justice of India
options.d: Only a retired Chief Justice of High Court

explanation: Explanation: • • • • • National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) was established in 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. The Chairman must be a retired Chief Justice of India. It also has four ex-officio members — heads of National Commissions for SCs, STs, Minorities, and Women. Members are appointed by the President based on recommendations of a committee including PM, Speaker, Home Minister, etc. Tenure is 5 years or up to age 70, whichever is earlier; not eligible for further govt employment. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Who among the following was never the Lok Sabha Speaker?
explanation: Explanation: • K.V.K. Sundaram — Not a Speaker; he was India’s first Law Secretary and 2nd Chief Election Commissioner (1958–67). • G.S. Dhillon — Speaker of 4th & 5th Lok Sabha (1969–75). • Baliram Bhagat — Speaker of 5th Lok Sabha (1976–77). • Hukum Singh — Speaker from 1962–67; admitted the first No-Confidence Motion. • This question tests factual recall of Lok Sabha Speakers’ list. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following events: 1. Fourth general elections in India 2. Formation of Haryana State 3. Mysore named as Karnataka State 4. Meghalaya and Tripura become full States Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the above?
explanation: Explanation: • Haryana Formation (1966) – carved out of Punjab on 1 November 1966. • Fourth General Elections (1967) – held in February 1967; marked political shifts. • Meghalaya & Tripura Statehood (1972) – became full-fledged states on 21 January 1972. • Mysore renamed Karnataka (1973) – officially renamed in 1973. • This sequence reflects post-independence state reorganization and political development chronology. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: The provisions in the Fifth Schedule and Sixth Schedule in the Constitution of India are made in order to

options.a: protect the interests of Scheduled Tribes
options.c: determine the powers, authorities, and responsibilities of Panchayats
options.d: protect the interests of all the border States

explanation: • • Fifth Schedule: safeguards Scheduled Areas/Tribes in non-Northeast regions. Sixth Schedule: deals with Autonomous District Councils in NE (Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram). Aim: protect cultural identity, selfgovernance, prevent exploitation. President has power to declare Scheduled Areas. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: With reference to the Union Government consider the following statements. 1. The Department of Revenue is responsible for the preparation of Union Budget that is presented to the parliament 2. No amount can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India without the authorization of Parliament of India. 3. All the disbursements made from Public Account also need the Authorization from the Parliament of India Which of the following statements given above is/ are correct?
explanation: • Budget is prepared by the Department of Economic Affairs, not Revenue. • Article 266: Parliamentary authorization required for withdrawals from Consolidated Fund of India. • Public Account is operated by executive action — no parliamentary vote needed. • Dept. of Revenue mainly deals with tax collection. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Who/Which of the following is the Custodian of the Constitution of India?
explanation: • Supreme Court ensures that laws and executive actions are constitutional. • Exercises judicial review (Articles 13, 32, 131, 136 etc.). • Interprets and protects the basic structure of the Constitution. • Acts as guardian and ultimate interpreter. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Legislative Council of a state in India can be larger in size than half of the Legislative Assembly of that particular state. 2. The Governor of a state nominates the Chairman of Legislative Council of that particular state. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: • Legislative Council: max size 1/3rd of Legislative Assembly; cannot exceed half. • Chairman is elected by the Council itself, not nominated by Governor. • Ensures Assembly predominance in bicameral states. • Article 171 governs Council composition. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: “To uphold and protect the Sovereignty Unity and Integrity of India” is a provision made in the
explanation: • Article 51A(c) of Fundamental Duties: Uphold sovereignty, unity, integrity. • Added by 42nd Amendment (1976). • Duties serve as moral obligations for citizens. • Promote national unity and constitutional values. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: The fundamental object of Panchayati Raj system is to ensure which among the following? 1. People’s participation in development 2. Political accountability 3. Democratic decentralization 4. Financial mobilization Select the correct answer using the code given below
explanation: • 73rd Amendment: aimed at democratic decentralization and people’s participation in local governance. • Article 40 laid the basis for village panchayats. • Political accountability exists but is not the core object. • Financial mobilization is not the fundamental objective. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: The ideal of “Welfare State” in the Indian Constitution is enshrined in its
explanation: • DPSP (Part IV) guides the State to ensure social and economic welfare. • Based on principles of equality of opportunity, economic justice. • Non-justiciable but fundamental to governance (Article 37). • Inspired by Irish Constitution and Gandhian principles. Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: There is a Parliamentary System of Government in India because the

options.a: Lok Sabha is elected directly by the people
options.d: Council of Ministers is responsible to the Lok Sabha

explanation: • Article 75(3): Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to Lok Sabha. • This executive accountability is the essence of parliamentary system. • (a), (b), (c) are true statements but do not define the system. • Based on Westminster model. Hence, option (d) is correct. 3. The RajyaSabha cannot discuss the Annual Financial Statement. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? (a) 1 only (b) 1 and 2 only (c) 2 and 3 only (d) 1, 2 and 3 Answer: (b) • Money Bill: RS can only recommend amendments within 14 days; LS may accept/reject. • Demands for Grants: only Lok Sabha votes. • RS can discuss the Annual Financial Statement, but cannot vote on demands. • Reflects financial supremacy of Lok Sabha. Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following Statements regarding the DPSP/ Directive Principles of State Policy: 1. The Principles spell out the socio-economic democracy in the country 2. The provisions contained in these Principles are not enforceable by any court. Which of the statements given below are correct?
explanation: • DPSP aims at social & economic democracy through rights like livelihood, education, equality. • Non-justiciable under Article 37, but fundamental to governance. • Provide policy direction for welfare legislation. • Taken from Irish Constitution. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: When a bill is referred to a joint sitting both the Houses of the Parliament, has to be passed by

options.a: a simple majority of member present and voting
options.b: three-fourths majority of member present and voting

explanation: • Article 108: Joint sitting resolves deadlock; not applicable to constitutional amendments. • Decision by simple majority of members present and voting. • Speaker of Lok Sabha presides. • Used to resolve legislative deadlock between Houses. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Executive Power of the union of India is vested in the Prime Minister. 2. The Prime Minister is the ex officio Chairman of the Civil Services Board. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: • • • • Article 53: Executive power vests in the President, not PM. Cabinet Secretary is ex officio Chairman of Civil Services Board, not PM. PM heads Council of Ministers, but constitutional vesting is with President. Illustrates formal vs real executive. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: With reference to the ‘Gram Nyayalaya Act’ which of the following statements is/ are correct? 1. As per the Act, Gram Nyayalayas can hear only civil cases and not criminal cases. 2. The Act allows local social activities as mediators/ reconciliators. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
explanation: • Gram Nyayalayas Act, 2008 provides for mobile village courts for speedy, affordable justice in rural areas. • Gram Nyayalayas can try both civil and criminal cases as per First and Second Schedules of the Act. • They follow summary procedure to ensure quick disposal. • Act allows appointment of local social activists and lawyers as mediators/reconciliators to promote conciliation. • Presiding officer (Nyayadhikari) is a Judicial Magistrate First Class, appointed by the State Government. Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: The Parliament of India acquires the power to legislate on any item in the State List in the national interest if a resolution to that effect is passed by the

options.a: Lok Sabha by a simple majority of its total membership
options.b: Lok Sabha by a majority of not less than two-thirds of its total membership
options.c: Rajya Sabha by a simple majority of its total membership
options.d: Rajya Sabha by a majority of not less than twothirds of its members present and voting.

explanation: • Article 249 empowers Parliament to legislate on State List in national interest. • Requires Rajya Sabha resolution with twothirds of members present and voting. • Resolution remains valid for 1 year, can be renewed for 1 year at a time. • State legislatures can also make laws simultaneously, but Parliament’s law prevails in case of conflict. • This provision strengthens Centre’s legislative power during special circumstances. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following statements: 1. The minimum age prescribed for any person to be a member of Panchayat is 25 years. 2. A Panchayat reconstituted after premature dissolution continues only for the remainder period. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: • 73rd Amendment Act (1992) governs Panchayati Raj. • Minimum age to contest Panchayat election is 21 years, not 25. • Term of Panchayat: 5 years, but if dissolved earlier, reconstituted body continues for remainder of original term. • Fresh elections must be held within 6 months of dissolution. • Aimed at ensuring continuity of local governance. Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. A Bill pending in the Lok Sabha lapses on its prorogation 2. A Bill pending in the Rajya Sabha, which has not been passed by the Lok Sabha, shall not lapse on dissolution of the Lok Sabha Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
explanation: • Prorogation: ends a session, not the House → bills do not lapse on prorogation. • Dissolution applies only to Lok Sabha; Rajya Sabha is permanent. • Bills pending in Lok Sabha lapse on dissolution, but those pending in Rajya Sabha but not passed by Lok Sabha do not lapse. • Article 107–108 outline these rules. • Ensures continuity of business initiated in the Upper House. Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Chief Secretary in a State is appointed by the Governor of that State 2. The Chief Secretary in a State has a fixed tenure Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: • Chief Secretary is the topmost executive officer in the State administration. • Appointed by the Chief Minister, not Governor (though formally issued in Governor’s name). • No fixed tenure; serves at the pleasure of the CM. • • Position filled from senior IAS cadre, selected on seniority-cum-merit basis. Administrative Reforms Commission suggested 3–4 year tenure, but not implemented. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following reflects the most appropriate relationship between law and liberty?

Liberty: • Liberty can be seen from two perspectives– negative and positive. • Negative liberty: It is concerned with the inviolable area of non-interference and not with the conditions in society, i.e. absence of obstacles, barriers or constraints. • Positive liberty: Recognizes that one can be free only in society and not outside it, therefore it is the possibility of acting or the fact of acting in such a way as to take control of one’s life and realise one’s fundamental • Safeguards of Liberty: o Declaration of rights of the individuals: It is an important safeguard of liberty. subject: Indian Polity
question: If the President of India exercises his power as provided under Article 356 of the Constitution of a particular State, then

options.a: The Assembly of the State is automatically dissolved.
options.b: The powers of the Legislature of that State shall be exercisable by or under the authority of the Parliament.
options.c: Article 19 is suspended in that State.
options.d: The President can make laws relating to that State.

explanation: • The proclamation of the President’s Rule is also known as ‘State Emergency’ or ‘Constitutional Emergency’. • When the President’s Rule is imposed in a state, the President dismisses the state council of ministers headed by the chief minister and parliament passes the state bills and budgets. • Ground for declaration of President’s Rule in a State: o Article 356: The president has the authority to declare if he is satisfied that the state government cannot function in accordance with the Constitution’s provisions. (The President can act on the report of the governor or otherwise). o Article 365: If a state fails to give effect or comply with any direction from the Centre, then it is lawful for the president to impose president’s rule. Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: With reference to the election of the President of India, consider the following statements: 1. The value of the vote of each MLA varies from State to State. 2. subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following statements: 1. In the first Lok Sabha, the single largest party in the opposition was the Swatantra Party 2. In the Lok Sabha, a “Leader of the Opposition” was recognised for the first time in 1969. 3. In the Lok Sabha, if a party does not have a minimum of 75 members, its leader cannot be recognised as the Leader of the Opposition. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: • Sub-Theme: Leader of Opposition • Statement 1 is incorrect: The Communist Party of India (CPI) was the single largest opposition party in the First general Election. CPI won in 16 seats. The Indian National Congress (INC) won a landslide victory, winning 364 of the 489 seats and 45% of the total votes polled. Jawaharlal Nehru became the first democratically elected PM of the country. • Statement 2 is correct: In 1969, an official leader of the opposition was recognized for the first time. However, it was given statutory recognition in 1977. • Statement 3 is incorrect: In order to receive the status of opposition party and Consequent Leader of Opposition Tag a party should secure 10% of the total strength of the House i.e., 55 seats in the Lok Sabha. subject: Indian Polity
question: With reference to the Parliament of India, which of the following Parliamentary Committees scrutinize and report to the House whether the powers to make regulations, rules, sub-rules, by-laws, etc. conferred by the Constitution or delegated by the Parliament are being properly exercised by the Executive within the scope of such delegation?
explanation: • Sub-Theme: Parliamentary Committees • Committee on Subordinate Legislation: o Composition: 15 members from the Lok Sabha are nominated by the Speaker. A Minister is not nominated to this o Functions: Scrutinizes and reports to the House whether the powers to make regulations, rules, sub-rules, by-laws etc. conferred by the Constitution or delegated by Parliament are being properly exercised by the executive within the scope of such Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly shall vacate his/her office if he/she ceases to be a member of the assembly. 2. Whenever the Legislative Assembly is dissolved, the Speaker shall vacate his/her office immediately. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: • Sub-Theme: Speaker & Deputy Speaker of Assembly • Statement 1 is correct: The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly vacates his office in three cases: 1. If he ceases to be a member of the assembly; 2. Speaker Resigns by writing to the deputy speaker and vice versa and 3. Removed by the resolution passed by a majority of all the members of the assembly. • Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 179 provided that, whenever the Assembly is dissolved, the Speaker shall not vacate his office until immediately before the first meeting of the Assembly after the dissolution. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Parliament of India can place a particular law in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution of India. 2. The validity of a law placed in the Ninth Schedule cannot be examined by any court and no judgement can be made on it. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: • Sub-Theme: Judicial Review • Statement 1 is correct: The Ninth Schedule and Article 31-B of the Indian Constitution was added by the 1st Amendment (1951) to protect the laws included in it from judicial scrutiny on the ground of violation of fundamental rights. o A law receives protection under Article 31-B (validation of certain Acts and Regulations) once it is passed and inserted into the Ninth Schedule and is thus exempt from judicial review. • Statement 2 is incorrect: The mandate of ninth schedule is to prevent judicial scrutiny but according to the Kesavananda Bharati Case, 1973, any violation with the ‘basic structure’ of the Constitution is open to challenge. Laws after 24 April 1973 are open for judicial review by courts. o IR Coelho vs State of Tamil Nadu, 2007: the SC ruled that all laws (including those in the Ninth Schedule) would be open to Judicial Review if they violated the basic structure of the constitution. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which of the following are regarded as the main features of the “Rule of Law”? 1. Limitation of Powers 2. Equality before law 3. People’s responsibility to the Government 4. Liberty and civil rights Select the correct answer using the code given below:
explanation: • Sub-Theme: Rule of Law Statement 1 and 2 are correct: Rule of law: The concept of ‘equality before law’ as enshrined in Article 14 of Indian Constitution is taken from the concept of ‘Rule of Law’ propounded by A.V. Dicey. • Rule of law is a legal principle that states that a country should be ruled by the law rather than by the arbitrary actions of particular government officials. • The ‘Rule of Law’ has 3 fundamental principles: o Absence of arbitrary power o Equality before law o Primacy of individual rights • Statement 3 is incorrect: The government is responsible/accountable to the people and not the vice versa. Hence, option (c) is correct. •

subject: Indian Polity
question: Right to Privacy is protected as an intrinsic part of Right to Life and Personal Liberty. Which of the following in the Constitution of India correctly and appropriately imply the above statement?

explanation: • Sub-Theme: Right to Privacy • Article 21 of the Indian Constitution deals with the protection of life and personal liberty. subject: Indian Polity
question: In the context of any country, which one of the following would be considered as part of its social capital?

options.a: The proportion of literates in the population
options.b: The stock of its buildings, other infrastructure and machines
options.c: The size of population in the working age group
options.d: The level of mutual trust and harmony in the society

explanation: • Option (d) is correct: The term social capital was popularised by Robert. As per OECD, it can be defined as “networks together with shared norms, values and understandings that facilitate co-operation within or among groups”. • It consists of trust, mutual understanding, shared values and behaviour that bind together the members of a community and make cooperative action possible. Such interaction enables people to build communities, to commit themselves to each other, and to knit the social fabric. • Option (a) is incorrect: The proportion of literates in the population and the size of population in the working age group are the examples of human capital. • Option (b) is incorrect: The stock of its buildings, other infrastructure and machines is the example of physical capital. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Under which Schedule of the Constitution of India can the transfer of tribal land to private parties for mining be declared null and void?
explanation: • Sub-Theme: Articles and Schedules of Indian Constitution • Fifth Schedule: Deals with the provisions as to the Administration and Control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled. Article 244 (1) of the Constitution defines Scheduled Areas as the areas defined so by the President of India and are mentioned in the 5th schedule of the Constitution. • In the Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh & Ors (1997) judgment the Supreme Court held that the transfer of tribal land to private parties for mining was null and void under the Fifth Schedule. • Under the Fifth Schedule, the Governors can make regulations for peace & good government of Scheduled Areas after consulting the Tribal Advisory Council (TAC). • Such regulations may prohibit or restrict the transfer of land by or among members of the scheduled tribes, regulate the allotment of land to members of the scheduled tribes and regulate the business of moneylending in relation to the scheduled tribes. • Additional Information: o Third Schedule:

subject: Indian Polity
question: The Ninth Schedule was introduced in the Constitution of India during the prime ministership of:
explanation: • Sub-Theme: Articles and Schedules of Indian Constitution • Ninth Schedule: The Ninth Schedule of the Indian Constitution was added by the 1st Amendment (1951) to protect the laws included in it from judicial scrutiny on the ground of violation of fundamental rights. At this time, Jawaharlal Nehru was the Prime Minister of India. He remained in the office from the year 1947 to 1964. • This schedule deals with the provisions as to validation of certain Acts and Regulations of the state legislatures dealing with land reforms and abolition of the zamindari system and of the Parliament dealing with other matters. • Additional Information: Prime Ministership years: Lal Bahadur Shastri: 1964–1966; Indira Gandhi: 1966–1971 and 1980–1984; Morarji Desai: 1977–1979. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: In the context of polity, which one of the following would you accept as the most appropriate definition of liberty?

options.a: Protection against the tyranny of political rulers
options.c: Opportunity to do whatever one likes

explanation: • Sub-Theme: Key Words in the Preamble • “Opportunity to develop oneself fully” covers liberty fully, therefore, one may surmise that the purpose of ensuring ‘liberty’ is that one has no obstacles or hindrances to realise one’s full potential. • Additional Information: o “Protection against the tyranny of political rulers” is a partial definition and has a connotation more towards fundamental rights rather than liberty. o “Absence of restraint” only covers part of the definition of liberty. o Liberty does not mean ‘licence’ to do whatever one likes; it is to be enjoyed within the limitations mentioned in the Constitution itself. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which Article of the Constitution of India safeguards one’s right to marry the person of one’s choice?
explanation: • Sub-Theme: Right to Privacy • Article 21 of the Indian Constitution deals with the protection of Life and Personal Liberty. This very article safeguards one’s right to marry the person of one’s choice. In the famous Hadiya Case (2017), the Supreme Court held that, “The right to marry a person of one’s choice is integral to Article 21 (right to life and liberty) of the Constitution”. • Additional Information: o Article 19: related to protection of six rights regarding freedom of speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence & profession. o Article 25: deals with the freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion. o Article 29: related to the protection of language, script and culture of minorities. Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following statements: 1. The 44th Amendment to the Constitution of India introduced an article placing the election of the Prime Minister beyond judicial review. 2. The Supreme Court of India struck down the 99th Amendment to the Constitution of India as being violative of the independence of judiciary. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: • Sub-Theme: Important and Major Constitutional Amendments • Statement 1 is incorrect: The 44th Amendment removed several distortions introduced by the 42nd Amendment, but it did not introduce an article placing the election of the Prime Minister beyond judicial review. The 39th Amendment (10 August 1975) placed the election of the President, Vice President, Prime Minister and Speaker beyond judicial scrutiny (during Emergency). • Statement 2 is correct: The 99th Constitutional Amendment Act would have established the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC). In 2015, a five-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court by 4:1 majority struck down the NJAC as unconstitutional, upholding the collegium system. • Additional: Justice Khehar observed that the proposed NJAC violated the independence of judiciary. Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: With reference to the Constitution of India, consider the following statements: 1. No High Court shall have the jurisdiction to declare any central law to be constitutionally invalid. 2. An amendment to the Constitution of India cannot be called into question by the Supreme Court of India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: • Sub-Theme: Final Interpreter and Guardian of the Constitution • Statement 1 is incorrect: Though the 42nd Amendment Act (1976) curtailed the power of High Courts in judicial review, the 43rd Amendment Act (1978) restored the original position. Now High Courts have jurisdiction to declare any central law constitutionally invalid. • Statement 2 is incorrect: The Supreme Court is the final interpreter and guardian of the Constitution. In Kesavananda Bharati (1973) the SC laid down the basic structure doctrine, and thus constitutional amendments that violate the basic structure can be nullified by the SC. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1959 exempts several posts from disqualification on the grounds of ‘Office of Profit’. 2. The above-mentioned Act was amended five times. 3. The term ‘Office of Profit’ is well-defined in the Constitution of India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: • Sub-Theme: Qualification and Disqualification of Parliament • Statement 1 is correct: There is no bar on how many offices can be exempted from the purview of the law. In the past the Supreme Court held that the Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Amendment Act, 2006 exempting 55 offices occupied by members of Parliament from disqualification was constitutionally valid. • Statement 2 is correct: The Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1959 has been amended five times to expand the exempted list. • Statement 3 is incorrect: The term ‘office of profit’ is not defined in the Constitution or in the Representation of the People Act, 1951. Articles 102(1)(a) and 191(1)(a) mention it but do not define it. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: In India, which of the following review the independent regulators in sectors like telecommunications, insurance, electricity, ? 1. Ad Hoc Committee set up by the Parliament. 2. Parliamentary Department Related Standing Committee 3. Finance Commission 4. Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission 5. NITI Aayog Select the correct answer using the code given below.
explanation: • Sub-Theme: Parliamentary Committees Parliamentary Committee: Purpose is to study and address a wide range of issues and to keep an eye on how the executive is operating. There are permanent/standing committees and ad hoc committees. • Department Related Standing Committee: Elected or appointed periodically, they work on a continuous basis to secure more accountability of the Executive to the Parliament, particularly financial accountability. • Ad hoc committees: Created on an ad hoc basis as the need arises and dissolved after completing the assigned task. • Both the Parliamentary committees (ad hoc & standing) are responsible to review the independent regulators in sectors like telecommunications, insurance, electricity, etc. Hence, option (a) is correct. •

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following statements: 1. The motion to impeach a Judge of the Supreme Court of India cannot be rejected by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha as per the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968. 2. The Constitution of India defines and gives details of what constitutes ‘incapacity and proved misbehaviour’ of the Judges of the Supreme Court of India. 3. The details of the process of impeachment of the Judges of the Supreme Court of India are given in the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968. 4. If the motion for the impeachment of a Judge is taken up for voting, the law requires the motion to be backed by each House of the Parliament and supported by a majority of total membership of that House and by not less than two-thirds of total members of that House present and voting. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: • Sub-Theme: Removal of Judges • Statement 1 is incorrect: Under the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968, a removal motion signed by 100 members (Lok Sabha) or 50 members (Rajya Sabha) is to be given to the Speaker/Chairman. The Speaker has the discretion to accept or reject the motion. • Statement 2 is incorrect: The Constitution does not define or give details of what constitutes ‘incapacity and proved misbehaviour’ of Judges — these are grounds but not exhaustively defined in the Constitution. • Statement 3 is correct: The details of the process of impeachment of the Judges of the Supreme Court of India are governed by the Judges Enquiry Act (1968). • Statement 4 is correct: If the motion for impeachment is taken up for voting, the law requires that the motion be passed by a ‘special majority’ — majority of the total membership of the House and not less than two thirds of members present and voting. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: With reference to the Constitution of India, prohibition or limitations or provisions contained in ordinary laws cannot act as prohibitions or limitations on the constitutional powers under Article 142. It could mean which one of the following.

options.a: The decisions taken by the Election Commission of India while discharging its duties cannot be challenged in any court of law.
options.b: The Supreme Court of India is not constrained in the exercise of its powers by laws made by the Parliament.
options.c: In the event of a grave financial crisis in the country, the President of India can declare a Financial Emergency without the counsel from the Cabinet.
options.d: State Legislatures cannot make laws on certain matters without the concurrence of the Union Legislature.

explanation: • Sub-Theme: Jurisdiction and Powers of Supreme Court • Article 142 deals with the enforcement of decrees and orders of the Supreme Court and empowers it to pass such orders as necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it. • The Supreme Court, in exercise of its jurisdiction, may pass orders which cannot be constrained by ordinary statutes — hence laws made by Parliament do not constrain the SC in exercise of Article 142 powers (e.g., Union Carbide Case, 1989 where SC invoked Article 142). • Additional Information: o ECI decisions can be challenged in High Courts and Supreme Court. o Article 360 empowers the President to proclaim Financial Emergency, but it requires Parliamentary approval. o Article 196 allows State Legislatures to make laws on State List and Concurrent List matters as per Constitution. Hence, option (b) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: With reference to the Legislative Assembly of a State in India, consider the following statements: 1. The Governor makes a customary address to Members of the House at the commencement of the first session of the year. 2. When a State Legislature does not have a rule on a particular matter, it follows the Lok Sabha rule on that matter. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: • Sub-Theme: Legislative Powers of Governor • Statement 1 is correct: Article 176(1) states that, through the legislative powers of the Governor, he can address the state legislature at the commencement of the first session after each general election and the first session of each year. • Statement 2 is incorrect: The State legislature is a constitutional body and derives its power from the Constitution. As per Article 208(1) a House of the Legislature of a State may make rules for regulating its procedure and the conduct of its business — there is no provision that it follows Lok Sabha rules when it lacks a rule. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Which one of the following suggested that the Governor should be an eminent person from outside the State and should be a detached figure without intense political links or should not have taken part in politics in the recent past?

options.d: National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (2000)

explanation: • Sub-Theme: Centre’s Control Over State Legislation • 1st ARC Recommendation (1966): Recommended appointment of persons having long experience in public life and administration and non-partisan attitude as governors. • Rajamannar Committee (1969): Recommended omission of the provision that the state ministry holds office during the pleasure of the Governor. • Sarkaria Commission (1983): Recommended that the Governor should be a distinguished outsider without intense political links, that he should not have recently participated in politics, and that he should not be a member of the ruling party. • National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (2000): Recommended that the President should appoint the governor only after consultation with the Chief Minister of that state. Hence, option (c) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: One common agreement between Gandhism and Marxism is

options.a: the final goal of a stateless society

explanation: • The common agreement between Gandhism and Marxism is the final goal of stateless and classless society. But means to achieve these final goals differ under Gandhism and Marxism. A stateless society refers to a society that lacks formal institutions of government. • Additional Information: o Karl Marx: State is an instrument of oppression and an organ of the bourgeoisie that only works for maintaining class dominance. Therefore, he strives for class struggle and revolution which will ultimately result in a stateless society. o Mahatma Gandhi: According to Gandhiji, even minimal state will require to use This was against nonviolence philosophy. Instead, Gandhiji was in favour of strengthening of local self-governments. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: In the context of India, which one of the following is the characteristic appropriate for bureaucracy?

options.a: An agency for widening the scope of parliamentary democracy
options.b: An agency for strengthening the structure of federalism
options.c: An agency for facilitating political stability and economic growth
options.d: An Agency for the implementation of public policy

explanation: • Bureaucracy Bureaucracy is the executive arm of the government, where the elected government employs competent state officials to run after state matters. They are selected by the government through the merit-based process. The major objective of bureaucracy in India has not been Parliamentary democracy’s expansion but rather the implementation of the decisions taken by the executive. • Parliamentary democracy results often in change at the helm of executive, the static and permanent bureaucracy provides continuity of policies and execution rather than political stability. Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Constitution of India defines its structure in terms of federalism, secularism, fundamental rights and democracy. 2. The Constitution of India provides for ‘Judicial review’ to safeguard the citizens’ liberties and to preserve the ideals on which the Constitution is based. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: • Sub-Theme: Basic Structure of Indian Constitution • Statement 1 is incorrect: Basic Structure encompasses basic and core values like federalism, secularism, fundamental rights and democracy which forms bedrock of the Indian Constitution. • Basic Structure cannot be amended by parliament under Art 368. • Basic Structure Doctrine is a Judicially innovative doctrine, and it was neither defined under Constitution nor it was defined by the Supreme Court or any other court. • Various judgments of the Supreme Court form the bedrock of Basic Structure Doctrine like: Kesavananda Bharati Case (24 April 1973) and IR Coelho vs State of Tamil Nadu, 2007. • Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 13 of the Indian Constitution though gives the power of judicial review but the word ‘judicial review’ is nowhere mentioned. The Union or the States shall not make any law that takes away or abridges any of the fundamental rights, and any law made in contravention of the aforementioned mandate shall, to the ext

question: The Preamble to the Constitution of India, is:

options.a: part of the Constitution but has no legal effect
options.b: not a part of the Constitution and has no legal effect either

explanation: • The doctrine of Separation of Powers entails the division of the legislative, executive, and judicial functions of government among different branches. • This demarcation prevents the concentration of excessive power by any branch of the Government. • It thus helps to safeguard the liberty and rights of the people in a democracy. • In the Directive Principles of State Policy, Article 50 mentions separation of judiciary from the executive. • Additional Information: o Committed Judiciary: It means a judiciary committed to the policies of the government or ruling party; thus, it can’t protect the liberty of all people. o Centralization of Power: Liberaldemocratic theory assumes that decentralization promotes democratic participation, especially local self-government. o Elected Government: Only having an elected government doesn’t safeguard liberty in liberal democracy. e.g., Pakistan. Hence, option (d) is correct.

question: What is the position of the Right to Property in India?

explanation: • Earlier, the Indian Constitution recognized the ‘Right to Property’ as a fundamental right under Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31. • Later, Right to Property as a fundamental right was abolished by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 and made it a legal right under Article 300-A. • Article 300-A of the Constitution states that “No person shall be deprived of his property save by Authority of Law”. • Thus, Right to Property in India is a legal right available to any person. Hence, option (b) is correct.

explanation: • Article 21 of the Indian Constitution deals with the protection of life and personal liberty. question: In the Government of India Act 1919, the functions of Provincial Government were divided into “Reserved” and “Transferred” subjects. explanation: • Government of India Act 1919 (MontaguChelmsford Reforms) came into force in 1921 to ensure Indian representation in the government. • It introduced ‘Dyarchy’, dividing provincial subjects into ‘Reserved’ and ‘Transferred’ categories. • Reserved Subjects (1, 3, and 4) included Law and Order, Finance, Land Revenue, Administration of Justice, Police, Irrigation, etc., administered by the Governor through his executive council of bureaucrats. • Transferred Subjects (2) such as Education, Health, Local Self-Government, Industry, Agriculture, Excise, etc., were handled by ministers nominated from elected members. • Other key provisions: Bicameralism, Direct Elections, Separation of Central and Provincial Budgets, Public Service Commission, and Communal Representation. Hence, option (d) is correct.

question: In essence, what does ‘Due Process of Law’ mean?
explanation: Explanation: • The Doctrine of ‘Due Process of Law’ has its origins in the English Common Law. It was first seen in the Magna Carta—the law of the Land for England. The due process of law doctrine examines not only whether a law exists to deprive a person of his or her life and personal liberty but also whether the legislation is fair, just, and not arbitrary. Unlike the Procedure established by Law where the judiciary assesses the procedure of the legislation and its competence only, the Supreme Court, in case of due process of law, analyses the procedure and the rationale of the law. It judges its reasonability. Hence option c is correct.

explanation: Explanation: • About the Constitution of India: o A constitution is a body of basic laws and principles that describes the general organisation and operation of the state and contains fundamental principles and norms that underlie and guide all government action. o A constitution is simultaneously a legal, political, and social instrument. question: As per Article 368 of the Constitution of India, the Parliament may amend any provision of the Constitution by way of: 1. Addition 2. Variation 3. Repeal Select the correct answer using the code given below:
explanation: Explanation: • Part XX of the Constitution deals with the provisions related to the amendment of the Constitution. According to Article 368, Parliament may, in the exercise of its constituent power, amend by way of addition, variation, or repeal any provision of this Constitution in accordance with the procedure laid down in this article. Thus, Options 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Hence option d correct.

subject: Indian Polity
question: Consider the following statements: 1. It is the Governor of the State who recognises and declares any community of that State as a Scheduled Tribe. 2. A community declared as a Scheduled Tribe in a State need not be so in another State. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Explanation: • Statement 1 is incorrect: According to Article 342(1), the President may, with respect to any State or Union Territory, and where it is a State, after consultation with the Governor, by a public notification, specify the tribes or tribal communities (or parts/groups) as Scheduled Tribes in relation to that State or UT. Parliament may by law include or exclude tribes from the list specified in such a notification. • Statement 2 is correct: The list of Scheduled Tribes is State/UT specific, and a community declared as a Scheduled Tribe in one State need not be so in another State. Hence option b correct.

question: With reference to Union Budget, consider the following statements: 1. The Union Finance Minister on behalf of the Prime Minister, lays the Annual Financial Statement before both the Houses of Parliament. 2. At the Union level, no demand for a grant be made except on the recommendation of the President of India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Explanation: • The term ‘budget’ is the popular name for the ‘Annual Financial Statement’ dealt with in Article 112. It is a statement of estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India for a financial year (1 April to 31 March). • Statement 1 is incorrect: The President shall cause to be laid before both Houses a statement of estimated receipts and expenditure. The Union Finance Minister, on behalf of the President, lays the Annual Financial Statement before both Houses of Parliament. • Statement 2 is correct: No demand for a grant shall be made except on the recommendation of the President. Hence option b correct.

question: With reference to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, consider the following statements: While any resolution for the removal of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is under consideration: 1. He/she shall not preside. 2. He/She shall not have the right to speak. 3. He/She shall not be entitled to vote on the resolution in the first instance. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Explanation: • Each House of Parliament has its own presiding officer. The Speaker is elected by the Lok Sabha from among its members. • When a resolution for the removal of the Speaker is under consideration, he cannot preside at the sitting of the House, though he may be present. However, he can speak and take part in the proceedings at such a time and vote in the first instance, though not in the case of an equality of votes. • Thus, Statement 1 is correct, and Statements 2 and 3 are incorrect. Hence option a correct.

question: With reference to the Indian Parliament, consider the following statements: 1. A bill pending in the Lok Sabha lapses on its dissolution. 2. A bill passed by the Lok Sabha and pending in the Rajya Sabha lapses on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha. 3. A bill in regard to which the President of India notified his/her intention to summon the Houses to a joint sitting lapses on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Explanation: • When the Lok Sabha is dissolved, all business pending before it or its committees lapses and must be reintroduced in the newly • • • • constituted Lok Sabha, except some specified items. A bill pending in the Lok Sabha lapses (whether it originated there or was transmitted by the Rajya Sabha). Thus, Statement 1 is correct. A bill passed by the Lok Sabha but pending in the Rajya Sabha lapses on dissolution. Thus, Statement 2 is correct. A bill not passed by the two Houses due to disagreement and if the President has notified intention to summon a joint sitting before the dissolution, does not lapse. Thus, Statement 3 is incorrect. Additional notes: A bill pending in the Rajya Sabha but not passed by the Lok Sabha does not lapse; a bill passed by both Houses but pending the President’s assent does not lapse; a bill returned by the President for reconsideration does not lapse. Hence option b correct.

question: With reference to the Parliament of India, consider the following statements: 1. Prorogation of a House by the President of India does not require the advice of the Council of Ministers. 2. Prorogation of a House is generally done after the House is adjourned sine die but there is no bar to the President of India prorogating the House which is in session. 3. Dissolution of the Lok Sabha is done by the President of India, who, save in exceptional circumstances, does so on the advice of the Council of Ministers. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Explanation: • Statement 1 is incorrect: The President prorogues a House on the advice of the Council of Ministers. • • Statement 2 is correct: The presiding officer declares the House adjourned sine die when business is completed; the President then issues a notification for prorogation. The President may also prorogue the House while in session. Statement 3 is correct: Rajya Sabha is a permanent House and is not subject to dissolution. Only the Lok Sabha is subject to dissolution, which is done by the President, who, save in exceptional circumstances, acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers. Hence option c correct.

Directorate General of Systems and Data Management: Carries out big data analytics to assist tax officers, under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance. explanation: Explanation: • Row I (Incorrect): The Directorate of Enforcement (ED) enforces the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, but it functions under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, not the Ministry of Home Affairs. • Row II (Correct): The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) enforces the Customs Act, • 1962, and operates under the CBIC, within the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance. Row III (Incorrect): The Directorate General of Analytics and Risk Management (DGARM) handles big data analytics, while the Directorate General of Systems and Data Management manages IT systems for customs and GST. Hence option a correct.

question: Consider the following statements (Panchayati Raj System): 1. Panchayats at the intermediate level exist in all States. 2. To be eligible to be a Member of a Panchayat at the intermediate level, a person should attain the age of thirty years. 3. The Chief Minister of a State constitutes a commission to review the financial position of Panchayats at the intermediate levels. Which of the statements given above are not correct?
explanation: Explanation: • Statement I (Incorrect): Article 243B allows exceptions for states with population below 20 lakhs, which need not establish intermediate Panchayats. • Statement II (Incorrect): As per Article 243F(1)(a), the minimum age is 21 years, not 30. • Statement III (Incorrect): Article 243-I empowers the Governor, not the Chief Minister, to constitute a State Finance Commission every five years. Hence option d correct.

question: Consider the following statements about Lokpal: 1. The power of Lokpal applies to public servants of India, but not to the Indian public servants posted outside India. 2. The Chairperson shall not be a Member of the Parliament and only the Chief Justice of India has to be its Chairperson. 3. The Chairperson or a Member shall not be a person of less than forty-five years of age. 4. Lokpal cannot inquire into the allegations of corruption against a sitting Prime Minister of India. Which of the statements given above is correct?

options.d: None of the above statements is correct

explanation: Explanation: • Statement I (Incorrect): The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 covers all public servants, both in India and abroad. • Statement II (Incorrect): The Chairperson need not be only the CJI; can be a former Supreme Court Judge or eminent person with 25 years of experience. • Statement III (Correct): Section 3(3)(c) mandates the Chairperson/Member must be at least 45 years old. • Statement IV (Incorrect): Lokpal can inquire against a sitting Prime Minister, except in matters of national security, with special safeguards. Hence option a correct.

question: Consider the following statements with regard to the pardoning power of the President of India: 1. The exercise of this power by the President can be subjected to limited judicial review. 2. The President can exercise this power without the advice of the Central Government. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Explanation: • • Statement I (Correct): As per Maru Ram v. Union of India and Epuru Sudhakar v. Govt. of A.P., judicial review applies if the decision is arbitrary or mala fide. Statement II (Incorrect): Under Article 74(1), the President must act on the advice of the Council of Ministers. Hence option a correct.

question: Consider the following statements about the Speaker of the Lok Sabha: 1. On the dissolution of the House of the People, the Speaker shall not vacate his/her office until immediately before the first meeting of the House of the People after the dissolution. 2. . According to the provisions of the Constitution of India, a Member of the House of the People on being elected as Speaker shall resign from his/her political Ammediately party 3. The Speaker of the House of the People may be removed from his/her office by a resolution of the House of the People passed by a majority of all the then Members of the House, provided that no resolution shall be moved unless at least fourteen days' notice has been given of the intention to move the resolution. Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Explanation: • Statement I (Correct): Article 94 (2nd proviso) allows the Speaker to continue until the new House meets. • Statement II (Incorrect): The Tenth Schedule exempts the Speaker from disqualification; no resignation from the party required. • Statement III (Correct): As per Article 94(c), removal requires an effective majority (majority of all then members) with 14 days’ notice. Hence option c correct.

explanation: Explanation: • Statement I (Incorrect): Paragraph 6(1) gives the power to Speaker/Chairman, not the President. • Statement II (Incorrect): The term “political party” appears multiple times in the Tenth Schedule, added by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985. Hence option d correct.

question: Consider the following statements about Minor Minerals: Statement I: In India, State Governments have no power for making rules for grant of concessions in respect of extraction of minor minerals even though such minerals are located in their territories. Statement II: In India, the Central Government has the power to notify minor minerals under the relevant law. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

options.a: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
options.b: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
options.c: Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
options.d: Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct

explanation: II is correct Explanation: • Statement I (Incorrect): Section 15(1) of the MMDR Act, 1957 empowers State Governments to make rules for minor minerals. • Statement II (Correct): Section 3(e) empowers the Central Government to declare any mineral as a minor mineral via notification. Hence option correct.

question: With reference to the Indian polity, consider the following statements (Ordinance-Making Power): 1. An Ordinance can amend any Central Act. 2. An Ordinance can abridge a Fundamental Right. 3. An Ordinance can come into effect from a back date. Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Explanation: • Statement I (Correct): Ordinances (Articles 123/213) have the same force as laws and can amend existing Acts. • Statement II (Incorrect): Ordinances are “law” under Article 13, cannot abridge Fundamental Rights. • Statement III (Correct): Ordinances can have retrospective effect, except in criminal matters (Article 20(1)). Hence option c correct.

explanation: Explanation: • Pair I (Correct): Itanagar (named after Ita Fort) and two National Parks – Namdapha and Mouling. • Pair II (Incorrect): Nagaland formed by State of Nagaland Act, 1962 (Parliamentary Act), not solely by Constitutional Amendment. • Pair III (Correct): Tripura – Part ‘C’ → UT (1956) → Statehood (1972) via North Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971. question: With reference to India, consider the following: 1. The Inter-State Council 2. The National Security Council 3. Zonal Councils How many of the above are established as per the provisions of the Constitution of India?
explanation: Explanation: • Inter-State Council (Constitutional): Established under Article 263. • National Security Council (Executive): Created by Executive Order. • Zonal Councils (Statutory): Created by States Reorganisation Act, 1956. Hence option a correct.

question: Consider the following statements about Governor’s Discretionary Powers: 1. The Constitution explicitly mentions that in certain spheres the Governor acts in discretion. 2. The President of India can, of his/her own, reserve a bill passed by a State Legislature for his/her consideration without it being forwarded by the Governor of the State concerned. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Explanation: • Statement I (Correct): Article 163(1) and 163(2) specify the Governor’s discretionary powers. • Statement II (Incorrect): Only the Governor, not the President, can reserve a bill under Article 200. Hence option a correct.

explanation: Explanation: • Pair I (Correct): Article 50 – DPSP (Part IV). • • Pair II (Correct): Article 51A(f) – Fundamental Duty (Part IVA). Pair III (Correct): Article 24 – Fundamental Right (Part III). Hence option c correct.

question: With reference to the Constitution of India, if an area in a State is declared as Scheduled Area under the Fifth Schedule: 1. the State Government loses its executive power in such areas and a local body assumes total administration 2. the Union Government can take over the total administration of such areas under certain circumstances on the recommendations of the Governor Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Explanation: • Statement I (Incorrect): The State retains executive power; Governor has special powers under Fifth Schedule. • Statement II (Incorrect): The Union may give directions, but cannot take over administration except via Article 356. Hence option d correct.

question: With reference to India, consider the following pairs : Organization Union Ministry I. The National Automative Board : Ministry of Commerce and Industry II. The Coir Board : Ministry of Heavy Industries III. The National Centre for Trade Information : Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises How many of the above pairs are correctly matched :
explanation: • The National Automotive Board (NAB) is set up to promote and develop the automotive sector in India. It falls under the Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises, not the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. Hence, Pair I is not correctly matched. • The Coir Board is a statutory body established for the promotion and development of coir and coir products in India. • It works under the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), not the Ministry of Heavy Industries. Hence, Pair II is not correctly matched. • The National Centre for Trade Information (NCTI) is an autonomous institution that provides trade information and market intelligence. • It functions under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, not the Ministry of MSME. Hence, Pair III is not correctly matched. Hence option d is the correct answer.

question: For a constitutional amendment, ratification by at least half of the States is required for changes relating to: I. List I-Union List, in the Sevent Schedule II. Extent of executive power of a State III. Conditions of Governor’s office For a constitutional amendment with respect to which of the above, ratification by the Legislatures of not less than one-half of the States is required before presenting the bill to the President of India for assent?
explanation: Explanation: • I (Correct): Seventh Schedule Lists affect Union–State legislative relations. • • II (Correct): Executive power (Articles 73 & 162) mentioned in Article 368(2) proviso. III (Incorrect): Governor’s conditions (Art. 158) not in proviso, amended by special majority alone. Hence option a correct.

question: With reference to the Indian polity, consider the following statements 1. The Governor is not answerable to any court for official acts. 2. No criminal proceedings shall be instituted or continued against the Governor during his term. 3. Members of a State Legislature are immune from court proceedings for anything said within the House. Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Explanation: • Statement I (Correct): Article 361(1) – Governor’s immunity from legal action. • Statement II (Correct): Article 361(2) – Absolute immunity from criminal proceedings. • Statement III (Correct): Article 194(2) – Freedom of speech in Legislature with legal immunity. Hence option d correct.
